rows.name: Read and talk about Roald Dahl stories
rows.unit: Unit 1 – Story Writing with Roald Dahl
steps: Gather the Roald Dahl books and seat the children in a circle where all can see the pages.
Read stories by Roald Dahl aloud to the group.
Hold a comprehension talk, asking who, what, where and what happened next.
Invite each child to read part of the story aloud, a page at a time, while the others follow.
Note how each child reads and which questions they answer.
rows.materials: Stories by Roald Dahl (e.g., Matilda, Danny the Champion of the World, Charlie and the Chocolate Factory)

levels.0: Page reading stops at most words and answers to questions about the story are absent or unrelated to what was read.
levels.1: With the educator reading alongside, a Dahl page is read and one question is answered after a prompt.
levels.2: A full Dahl page is read aloud fluently and questions about characters and events are answered correctly after listening.
levels.3: A Dahl page is read with expression, and an answer to a question includes a reason or a link to another story.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B4

rows.name: Write a story based on a Roald Dahl character
rows.unit: Unit 1 – Story Writing with Roald Dahl
steps: Suggested: Remind the children of the Roald Dahl characters they have met and let each choose one.
Suggested: Ask each child to say in one sentence who the chosen character is.
Children write a story based on that character, in sentences of their own.
Suggested: Children reread the story and add one more detail to it.
Suggested: Pairs swap and read each other's stories aloud.

levels.0: Story is missing or copies lines from the book without any sentences of the writer's own.
levels.1: Chosen character is named and one or two sentences are written after the educator talks through ideas.
levels.2: A short story of several own sentences follows the chosen Dahl character, with a beginning and something that happens.
levels.3: Story gives the character a new adventure not found in the books, with details, a clear ending and reasons told aloud.

rows.name: Project 1 – Number Games
steps: Prepare number cards or a list of numbers up to 1,000 and give each child a slate or notebook.
Play a number game: the educator or a leader calls out a number and children write it in digits.
Children write the same number in words beside the digits.
Partners swap slates and check each other's digits and words.
Repeat for several rounds, moving to larger numbers, and share tricky ones with the class.

levels.0: Digits are reversed or mixed, such as 305 written as 3005, and no word forms are attempted.
levels.1: Numbers are written in digits correctly, but the words appear only after the educator shows number-name cards.
levels.2: Called numbers up to 1,000 appear in correct digits and correct words, such as 'four hundred twelve' beside 412.
levels.3: Own mystery numbers are set for partners, and both the digit and word forms are checked and corrected aloud.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!C4

rows.name: Project 2 – Surprising sums, Shopkeeper's Ledger
steps: Set up a pretend shop with items, price tags, play coins and notes, and an inventory list.
Children list each item and its quantity in a ledger.
Run pretend sales: one child buys, one sells, and each transaction is recorded in the ledger.
Use addition, subtraction and multiplication to update stock and money totals in the ledger.
Partners check each other's ledger against the shop's coins and stock, then share the day's total.

levels.0: Ledger has blank rows or lists items without quantities, and coin totals are miscounted.
levels.1: Stock and sales are entered after the educator models the first row, and coins are added by counting up together.
levels.2: Ledger shows stock, each sale and a correct money total from coins or notes, with additions matching the cash.
levels.3: Ledger totals are checked by a second method and a mistake found in a partner's entry is explained aloud.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!C4

rows.name: Tally Hunt
steps: Walk around the campus noting different objects, such as the colours of cars.
Record each one with a tally mark in a table.
Count the tallies for each kind of object.
Tell a partner which kind was seen most.

levels.0: Tally marks are drawn without grouping, so the totals for each colour cannot be read without recounting from one.
levels.1: Makes tally marks for objects only with the educator calling out each sighting; totals need help.
levels.2: Records each sighting with a tally mark and writes the total for every kind.
levels.3: Runs a tally for a new thing on the campus and explains which total is biggest and why.

rows.name: ‘सवेरा’ – कविता लेखन, चित्र निर्माण और शीर्षक
steps: कविता ‘सवेरा’ पढ़ें।
बातचीत करें कि कविता में सुबह के कौन-से दृश्य और आवाज़ें हैं।
कविता-लेखन करें।
चित्र बनाएँ और शीर्षक दें।
अपनी कविता साथी या कक्षा को सुनाएँ।

levels.0: Poem lines are copied from ‘सवेरा’ with no new words, or only a title and a drawing appear.
levels.1: Two or three own lines are written after the educator and a partner suggest rhyming words aloud.
levels.2: Own poem of several lines about morning appears with a title and a matching drawing.
levels.3: Poem uses new rhymes or describing words not found in ‘सवेरा’, and the writer explains why the title was chosen.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D4

rows.name: ‘नीलम परी’ – कहानी वाचन, अनुभव लेखन, चित्र वर्णन
steps: कहानी ‘नीलम परी’ का वाचन करें, समूह में बारी-बारी से।
कहानी में क्या हुआ, इस पर बातचीत करें।
अपने अनुभव का लेखन करें।
चित्र का वर्णन करें।
अपना लेखन साथी को सुनाएँ।

levels.0: Group reading is silent or skips whole lines, and the written piece does not connect to any experience of their own.
levels.1: Own turn in the group reading goes with the educator pointing to words, and one sentence about an experience is written.
levels.2: Own lines of ‘नीलम परी’ are read aloud in turn, and a few sentences describe a real experience linked to the story.
levels.3: Experience writing links a story event to own life with reasons, and is read aloud with expression to the group.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D4

rows.name: मराठी श्लोक, गाणी, खेळ
steps: मुलांना वर्तुळात बसवा आणि आजचा श्लोक व गाणे सांगा.
मराठी श्लोक म्हणा.
मराठी गाणी म्हणा.
मराठी खेळ खेळा.
प्रत्येक मुलाने एक ओळ किंवा कडवे म्हणावे आणि इतरांनी ऐकावे.

levels.0: Lips stay still or only a few words are said during the shloka, even when the whole group recites together.
levels.1: Shloka lines are said along with the group, following the educator's lead, with several words missed.
levels.2: A shloka or song is recited aloud from memory, with most words in the right order and a steady rhythm.
levels.3: Group recitation is led, with the meaning of a line explained in own words and the tune kept steady.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D4

rows.name: मुलांचा परिचय व नाव लिहिण्याचा प्रयत्न
steps: मुलांना वर्तुळात बसवा आणि शिक्षक स्वतःचा परिचय देतात.
मुले आपला परिचय देतात.
आपले नाव लिहिण्याचा प्रयत्न करतात.
लिहिलेले नाव मित्राला दाखवून वाचून दाखवतात.

levels.0: Name card shows scribbles or letters from another script, with no Devanagari letters of the name.
levels.1: Name is written in Devanagari only by copying from a card, with some letters reversed or missing.
levels.2: Own name is written in Marathi from memory, with every letter formed and in the right order.
levels.3: Names of a friend or family member are also written in Marathi, and the letters are named aloud.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D4

rows.name: प्रोजेक्ट – मैं और मेरा परिवार (helpers poster)
steps: बच्चे उन लोगों के चित्र बनाते हैं जो उनकी देखभाल या मदद करते हैं (नाम या घर की जानकारी लिखे बिना)।
Suggested: हर चित्र के नीचे एक हिंदी वाक्य लिखते हैं कि वह व्यक्ति क्या काम करता है।
Suggested: चार्ट पर चित्र चिपकाकर कक्षा में पोस्टर दिखाते हैं।

levels.0: Poster has drawings but no Hindi sentences, or sentences are copied without relating to the helpers.
levels.1: Drawings of helpers members appear with sentences written after the educator scribes the first one.
levels.2: Poster holds drawings of helpers members, each with a Hindi sentence naming or describing that person.
levels.3: Poster adds details such as something the helpers does together, with several Hindi sentences and a spoken explanation.

rows.name: Cotton vs Soil Challenge
steps: Set up the two growing conditions, cotton and soil, with the same seeds in each, and label them.
Ask the children to predict which will grow better and why.
Take part in the Cotton vs Soil Challenge: give both set-ups water and keep them somewhere suitably warm.
Observe each day and record what changes with drawings or short notes.
Discuss what the plants needed and share the evidence from the notes.

levels.0: Observation sheet is blank or records only what the pots look like, with no mention of water or warmth.
levels.1: Water is named as a need after the educator asks what was added each day, with no evidence cited.
levels.2: Statement that plants need water and suitable temperature is backed by a recorded observation, such as which pot grew.
levels.3: Evidence from both set-ups is compared to predict what a new plant would need, explained in own words.

rows.name: Reading project
steps: Introduce the Reading project and let each child choose a book to read.
Give regular time to read the chosen book.
Children look at the cover and note a few sentences to say about the book.
Each child presents the book to the class, showing the cover.
Classmates ask one question after each presentation.

levels.0: Book is held up but the title is not named, and no sentence about the story is said.
levels.1: Cover is shown and the title read, with a sentence about the book given after the educator asks a prompt question.
levels.2: Presentation shows the cover and gives a few sentences about the book, including its title and what happens.
levels.3: Book presentation adds a favourite part with a reason and answers a classmate's question about the story.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!I4

rows.name: Everyday journal writing
steps: Introduce everyday journal writing and give each child a journal notebook.
Talk briefly about the day: what we did and who was there.
Children write the date and a journal entry about their day in sentences of their own.
Children reread the entry and fix capital letters and full stops.
Volunteers read an entry aloud to the group.
rows.time_note: Home - every day, from the start of June

levels.0: Journal page holds a date or drawing only, with no sentence about the day.
levels.1: One sentence about the day is written after the educator asks what happened first.
levels.2: Journal entry holds several own sentences about events of the day, in order, with capital letters and full stops.
levels.3: Entry includes feelings and reasons about the day's events, and the writer explains a word choice when asked.

rows.note: named in Routines!B5

rows.name: Think Outside the Box (Thursday)
steps: Introduce Think Outside the Box as the Thursday routine and put a problem on the board.
Children think quietly for a minute, then talk with a partner.
Each pair shares ideas, aiming for ones that are unusual.
Record the ideas on a class chart.
Talk about which idea was most unusual and why it could work.
rows.time_note: Home - Thursday, from June, first week

levels.0: Ideas offered repeat the common answer already given, or no idea is shared when the problem is set.
levels.1: An unusual idea is offered only after a partner's suggestion is built on or the educator gives a hint.
levels.2: A solution different from the usual ones is shared, such as using an object in a new way.
levels.3: Several unusual solutions are given and the reason each could work is explained aloud.

rows.note: named in Routines!B7

rows.name: Word of the Week (Friday)
steps: Write the Word of the Week on the board, say it, and have the children repeat it.
Explain the meaning with an example from the children's day.
Children say a sentence with the word to a partner.
Children write their own sentence using the word.
Share a few sentences with the class.
rows.time_note: Home - Friday, from June, third week

levels.0: Sentence leaves out the word or uses it in a way that does not match its meaning.
levels.1: Word is placed in a sentence only when the educator gives the sentence start, such as 'I felt ...'.
levels.2: Sentence uses the week's word correctly and makes sense, in a sentence of own making.
levels.3: Word is used in two different sentences, and its meaning is explained in own words.

rows.note: named in Routines!B6

rows.name: Weekly Math Challenge (Friday)
steps: Introduce the Friday Weekly Math Challenge and choose a problem on a topic taught that week.
Read the problem aloud together and underline the numbers.
Children work on the problem on their own in their notebooks.
Pairs compare methods and answers.
Share an answer and the method with the class.
rows.time_note: Home - Monday, from July, first week (the 2026-27 planner says Friday: conflict)

levels.0: Notebook shows numbers copied from the problem but no operation or answer attempted.
levels.1: Problem is solved after the educator rereads it aloud and asks which operation to use.
levels.2: Challenge problem is solved with a shown working line and a correct answer on a topic taught.
levels.3: Answer is reached by a working line, and a second method is described or a similar problem is made up.

rows.note: named in Routines!B8

rows.name: Newspaper magazine
steps: Introduce the Newspaper magazine routine and hand out copies of RobinAge.
Children browse and each choose one news item.
Pairs read the chosen item together.
Each child tells one news item to a partner, saying what happened.
A few children share their item with the whole class.
rows.time_note: School timetable, once a fortnight, from July first week

levels.0: News item is pointed to in the magazine but nothing is said about what it was about.
levels.1: Headline is read out and one fact is told after the educator asks 'what happened?'.
levels.2: One news item from RobinAge is told in a few spoken sentences saying what happened.
levels.3: Who, where and why of a news item are told, and a question is asked of the listener.

rows.note: named in Routines!B10

rows.name: Novel reading
steps: Introduce the Novel Reading routine and settle the class with the novel.
Read a chapter aloud, or let children read it in turns.
Pause at key points and ask what has happened so far.
After the chapter, children tell a partner what it was about in their own words.
A few children share their retelling with the class.
rows.time_note: School timetable, from July fourth week

levels.0: Retelling stops after the chapter's title or repeats lines read aloud word for word.
levels.1: Chapter events are told in short pieces when the educator asks 'then what?', with some events missing.
levels.2: Chapter is retold in own words, with the main events in order and the main characters named.
levels.3: Retelling adds a prediction of what comes next, with a reason taken from the chapter.

rows.note: named in Routines!B9

rows.name: Looking at celebrations
steps: Collect pictures of celebrations that the children know and display them.
Suggested: Look at celebrations together: show one picture and ask what children can see.
Suggested: Each child says one thing people do at the celebration shown.
Suggested: Children share how their own family celebrates.
Suggested: Compare the pictures and note what is similar and different.

levels.0: Picture is looked at but nothing is said about what people are doing in it.
levels.1: A thing people do is named after the educator points to part of the picture and asks.
levels.2: One thing people do at a known celebration is said clearly, drawn from the picture shown.
levels.3: Several things people do are named and compared with how their own family celebrates.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B9

rows.name: Write lists to plan a party
steps: Decide on a pretend party, or a dish to make, as a class.
Model writing a list on the board with one item on each line.
Children write lists of the things needed to plan the party.
Partners compare lists and add anything missing.
Share a few lists with the class.

levels.0: List holds a single item or runs on as a sentence instead of separate items for the party.
levels.1: Items are listed after the educator names categories, with some spellings copied from the board.
levels.2: List of party things needed has several items, one per line, each relevant to the party or dish.
levels.3: List is grouped under headings such as food and decorations, with quantities added.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B9

rows.name: Follow instructions; command verbs and sequencing verbs
steps: Give the class a simple set of instructions to follow, such as a drawing or craft task.
Read the instructions aloud together, in order.
Recognise the role of command verbs and sequencing verbs by underlining them in the instructions.
Children write two or three instructions of their own, each starting with a command verb.
Partners read each other's instructions aloud and follow them.

levels.0: Instruction steps are read out of order or skipped, and written steps begin with 'You' or 'I'.
levels.1: Steps are read in order with the educator pointing, and command verbs are picked out only with help.
levels.2: Instructions are read aloud in order and own written steps each start with a command verb such as 'cut' or 'fold'.
levels.3: Own multi-step instructions use command and sequencing words, and a partner follows them successfully.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B9

rows.name: Write an invitation
steps: Show a sample invitation and point out the date, time and place.
Agree the details of a pretend party, such as the day, the time and where it is.
Children write an invitation including the date, time and place.
Check the invitation against a list: greeting, date, time, place, name.
Swap with a partner, who reads it aloud to confirm nothing is missing.

levels.0: Invitation lacks date, time and place, or is a message with none of those details.
levels.1: One or two of date, time and place are written after the educator points to the checklist.
levels.2: Invitation to a party names date, time and place correctly, with a greeting and the writer's name.
levels.3: Invitation adds extra details such as what to bring, and a partner reading it finds no missing information.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B9

rows.name: Follow and write instructions: how to get from school to playground
steps: Walk the route from the classroom to the playground, or look at a simple route picture.
Follow spoken instructions from the educator to reach a place.
Write instructions for how to get from school to the playground, one step on each line.
Start each step with a command verb.
A partner follows the written instructions and says if any step is unclear.

levels.0: Route steps are written as one long sentence or describe places without any command verbs.
levels.1: Two route steps start with verbs like 'walk' after the educator models the first line.
levels.2: Route to the playground is written as ordered steps, each beginning with a command verb like 'turn' or 'walk'.
levels.3: Directions include landmarks and sequencing words, and a partner reaches the playground using only the written steps.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B9

rows.name: Revision worksheets: tables, place value, addition and subtraction
steps: Hand out the revision worksheets and base-ten blocks.
Revise tables 2 to 12 by chanting and quick oral questions.
Revise place value by building 3-digit numbers with blocks and naming hundreds, tens and ones.
Do the addition and subtraction worksheets.
Check answers in pairs and note the mistakes to revisit.

levels.0: Table facts are counted on fingers or skipped, and blocks show a different number of tens than the digit.
levels.1: Times-table facts for 2 and 10 come quickly, others need counting, and blocks need the educator's check.
levels.2: Tables 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 are said without counting, and base-ten blocks match the hundreds, tens and ones.
levels.3: Facts beyond 10 are recalled, and a block model is used to explain regrouping in a sum.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!C9

rows.name: ‘मीठा झगड़ा’ – संवाद
steps: कविता ‘मीठा झगड़ा’ पढ़ें।
देखें कि कविता में कौन-कौन बोल रहा है और किसकी कौन-सी पंक्ति है।
संवाद बोलें: दो-दो बच्चे जोड़ी में अपनी पंक्तियाँ बारी-बारी से बोलें।
जोड़ियाँ कक्षा के सामने संवाद प्रस्तुत करें।

levels.0: Lines of the dialogue are silent or spoken out of turn, with words that differ from the poem.
levels.1: Own lines are said when the partner or educator whispers the first words, in a flat voice.
levels.2: Spoken lines match the poem and are said in turn with a partner, in a clear voice.
levels.3: Dialogue is performed with expression and a change of voice for each speaker, then explained in own words.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D9

rows.name: ‘मीठा झगड़ा’ – अनुच्छेद-लेखन
steps: कविता ‘मीठा झगड़ा’ फिर से पढ़ें और पसंद आई पंक्तियाँ बताएँ।
कविता के बारे में अपनी राय बोलकर साथी को बताएँ।
अनुच्छेद-लेखन करें।
अनुच्छेद में कविता पर अपनी राय का एक वाक्य ज़रूर लिखें।
अनुच्छेद पढ़कर सुनाएँ।

levels.0: Paragraph retells lines of the poem but gives no sentence about liking it or any opinion.
levels.1: A sentence of opinion is written after the educator offers a starter such as ‘मुझे अच्छा लगा’.
levels.2: Paragraph contains a sentence giving own view of the poem, supported by a line read from it.
levels.3: Paragraph gives opinion with a reason, quoting a specific line, and compares it to another poem.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D9

rows.name: Separation of mixture experiment
steps: Prepare mixtures and tools such as a sieve, a filter and containers.
Ask the children to predict how each mixture could be separated.
Do the experiment: separate a mixture by hand or with a sieve, then filter a solid from a liquid.
Record what tool was used and what was left behind.
Share findings and what worked best.

levels.0: Mixture stays mixed after the attempt, or the tool chosen does not fit the materials.
levels.1: Sieve or hand picking is used correctly, with the educator holding the filter and guiding the pouring.
levels.2: A solid mixture is separated by hand or sieve and a solid-liquid mixture is filtered with clear liquid collected.
levels.3: Choice of hand, sieve or filter is explained for each mixture, and a new mixture is separated independently.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F9

rows.name: Cotton to cloth story sequencing cards
rows.unit: Fortnight 3 & 4: The Journey of Fabric (From Plant to Cloth)
steps: Gather the materials and set out the workspace.
Put the cotton-to-cloth story cards in order: harvesting, spinning, dyeing.
Role-play each step or make a simple storyboard.

levels.0: Story cards are laid out with spinning before harvesting, and the order is not explained.
levels.1: Harvest card goes first, but the rest need the educator to tap the next card.
levels.2: Cards run in order from harvesting to spinning to dyeing to cloth, and each card is named.
levels.3: Retells the journey from cotton plant to cloth in own words, using the cards as clues.

rows.name: Scratch: introduction to speech sprites
steps: Open Scratch on the available computers, with children in pairs.
Show how to add a sprite and snap on a say block.
Children use Scratch speech sprites to make a sprite say a line for a digital story.
Add another block or sprite to continue the story.
Run the scripts and share them with the class.

levels.0: Blocks are scattered in the coding area and the sprite does nothing when the flag is clicked.
levels.1: Sprite speaks after the educator drags the first block, with one more block added by the pair.
levels.2: Snapped blocks make a sprite say a line when run, and the script behaves as planned.
levels.3: Script chains several blocks so sprites speak in turn, and a block that fails is found and fixed.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F9

rows.name: Independence Day craft and art
steps: Gather paper, colours and craft materials.
Recall the art techniques the class has learned this year.
Children plan an Independence Day craft and artwork, choosing two techniques.
Make the Independence Day craft and art.
Display the work and let each artist say which two techniques were used.

levels.0: Artwork uses a single technique, or materials are used without a plan for the theme.
levels.1: Second technique appears only after the educator suggests it, giving a piece with one clear technique.
levels.2: Finished artwork for Independence Day shows two taught techniques chosen by the artist.
levels.3: Two techniques are named and the reason for each choice is explained, with details added by own design.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!G9

rows.name: Short essay + drawing
steps: Choose a topic together and talk about it.
Plan three ideas in order, first, next and last, with a quick sketch.
Write a short essay following the plan.
Draw a picture to go with the essay.
Read the essay aloud to a partner and check the order of ideas.
rows.time_note: School timetable, once a fortnight, from August

levels.0: Essay lines jump between ideas with no clear order, or only one sentence is written.
levels.1: Ideas are put in order after the educator numbers them on a plan, with a drawing alongside.
levels.2: Short essay presents ideas in a clear order of beginning, middle and end, with a matching drawing.
levels.3: Essay uses linking words to join ideas, and the writer explains why the order was chosen.

rows.note: named in Routines!B11

rows.name: Word of the week
steps: Choose the word of the week and display it on the board or a word wall.
Say the word together and clap its syllables.
Children use the word in spoken sentences with a partner.
Children write a sentence using the word in their notebooks.
Revisit the word at the end of the week and share sentences.

levels.0: Notebook line shows the word copied alone, without any sentence built around it.
levels.1: Spoken sentence with the word comes after a partner models one first, and writing needs help.
levels.2: Own written sentence contains the word of the week in the right sense and ends with a full stop.
levels.3: Word appears in a new context, such as a sentence about home, and a classmate's use of it is kindly corrected.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!I9

rows.name: Novel reading
steps: Gather the class and the novel for the Novel reading routine.
Read a chapter aloud, or let children read it in turns.
Talk about what happened and to whom.
Children retell the chapter to a partner in their own words.
Record the chapter read in a class reading log.

levels.0: Chapter talk contains only the book's title or a single word, with no events described.
levels.1: With a picture or the book's page open, one or two events are recalled after prompting.
levels.2: Own words explain what the chapter was about, including what happened and to whom, without reading it out.
levels.3: Chapter summary is given and compared with an earlier chapter, with reasons for a favourite part.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!I9

rows.name: Write a list of items to buy to make a dish
steps: Choose a dish the class knows and talk about what is needed to make it.
Children think about which of those items they would have to buy.
Each child writes a list of the items to buy, one item on each line.
Children read the list to a partner and check that nothing is missing.
A few children share their list with the class.

levels.0: List holds unrelated items or a single word, with none matching what the named dish needs.
levels.1: After a partner names the ingredients aloud, writes most of the list but leaves out items or needs spelling help.
levels.2: Writes a list of three or more items that suit the chosen dish, each on its own line.
levels.3: Adds quantities or sorts the list by shop section, and explains in own words why each item is needed.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B14

rows.name: Plan a new game for a party
steps: Put children in small groups and ask each group to think of a new game for a party.
Groups decide what the game needs and how it is played, and write a plan with the steps in order.
Each group practises telling the steps of the game aloud in order.
Groups present the plan to another group, who ask questions.
Groups improve the plan using what they heard.

levels.0: Group's plan names a game but lists no steps, or the steps given cannot be followed in sequence.
levels.1: Partners and educator prompting supply the steps, which the group tells in order with some gaps.
levels.2: Group tells the steps of their new game in order, from start to finish, using words like first and next.
levels.3: Changes a rule when peers try the game, and explains in own words why the new step order works better.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B14

rows.name: Write instructions with sequencing words and command verbs
steps: Choose a short everyday task and talk through what is done first, next and last.
Write instructions for the task, one step on each line.
Use sequencing words such as first, next and then, and begin each step with a command verb.
Swap with a partner, who follows the instructions exactly as written.
Fix any unclear step and read the final instructions aloud.

levels.0: Written steps read as full descriptive sentences such as 'You are mixing', with no command verbs and no sequencing words.
levels.1: With a verb word bank from the educator, starts some steps with a command verb but others with 'You' or a noun.
levels.2: Writes each step beginning with a command verb such as mix or fold, with first, next and then marking the order.
levels.3: Writes instructions for a new task using command verbs and sequencing words, then corrects a partner's step that lacks a verb.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B14

rows.name: ‘बदल गई सुहानी’ – संवाद-लेखन
steps: कहानी 'बदल गई सुहानी' पढ़ें।
कहानी के दो पात्र चुनें और सोचें कि वे आपस में क्या बात करेंगे।
संवाद-लेखन करें: हर पात्र का नाम लिखें और उसके आगे उसकी बात लिखें।
साथी के साथ दोनों पात्र बनकर संवाद को बोलकर पढ़ें।
कुछ जोड़ियाँ अपना संवाद कक्षा के सामने सुनाएँ।

levels.0: Dialogue lines hold no speaker names or come from one speaker only, so the text does not read as two characters talking.
levels.1: Pointing back to the story with an educator, writes a few lines for each character, though speaker labels are inconsistent.
levels.2: Writes a back-and-forth conversation with separate labelled lines for each character, and the replies fit the story.
levels.3: Adds a new scene of conversation in the characters' voices and reads it aloud with a partner taking the second role.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D14

rows.name: ‘बदल गई सुहानी’ – ग्रीटिंग कार्ड बनाना
steps: ग्रीटिंग कार्ड के लिए कागज़, रंग और पेंसिल तैयार रखें।
कार्ड पर एक चित्र बनाएँ और उसमें रंग भरें।
ग्रीटिंग कार्ड बनाएँ और चित्र के बारे में अपने वाक्य लिखें।
कार्ड साथी को दिखाएँ और लिखे वाक्य पढ़कर सुनाएँ।
कुछ कार्ड कक्षा में प्रदर्शित करें।

levels.0: Card holds only a picture or copied words, with no sentence of their own about the coloured picture.
levels.1: Partner or educator suggests what to say, and one short sentence about the colouring is written with spelling help.
levels.2: Two or more sentences in own words on the card describe what is in the coloured picture.
levels.3: Card's sentences give a reason or a feeling about the picture and are read out to the person it is meant for.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D14

rows.name: शब्द खेल गतिविधि
steps: बच्चों को दो टोलियों में बाँटें और खेल के नियम समझाएँ।
शब्द खेल खेलें: शिक्षक एक शब्द बोलें और बच्चे उसके समान अर्थ वाला शब्द बताएँ।
हर सही शब्द पर टोली को एक अंक दें।
खेल के बाद बच्चे कुछ शब्द और उनके समान अर्थ वाले शब्द कॉपी में लिखें।
कुछ बच्चे बताएँ कि उन्होंने कौन-से नए शब्द सुने।

levels.0: Offers the same word back or an opposite when asked for a पर्यायवाची, so no word with a matching meaning is heard.
levels.1: Gives a पर्यायवाची for some words after the educator reads a clue or shows a picture, and stays silent on others.
levels.2: Says a word with the same meaning for each word called in the game, written or spoken correctly.
levels.3: Gives two or more पर्यायवाची for a word and explains in own words why they mean the same.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D14

rows.name: Shadow Detective Experiment
steps: Give each group a torch or other light source, an opaque object and a plain wall or sheet of paper to catch the shadow.
Do the Shadow Detective experiment: shine the light on the object so that its shadow falls on the wall or sheet.
Move the object closer to and further from the light and watch how the size of the shadow changes.
Move the light closer and further instead, and watch the shadow again.
Draw or tell what was seen in each case.
Groups share what they found and show a shadow to the class.

levels.0: Shadow does not appear on the surface, or object and light are placed so that no shadow can be seen.
levels.1: Once the educator holds the torch steady, a shadow forms and its size change is noticed only when pointed out.
levels.2: Makes a shadow with a chosen object and light, then makes it bigger and smaller by moving one of them.
levels.3: Predicts before moving whether the shadow will grow or shrink, tests it, and explains the result using distance in own words.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F14

rows.name: Scratch project: introduction to Scratch and block coding
steps: Open Scratch on each computer and look together at the sprite, the blocks and the coding area.
Do a Scratch project: drag command blocks into the coding area and snap them together.
Run the blocks and see the sprite move or say something.
Add a loop block so that the sprite repeats an action.
Try changing a block or adding a new sprite and see what changes.
Show the project to a partner and say what each block does.

levels.0: Blocks sit loose in the coding area, not snapped together, so the sprite does not move or change when run.
levels.1: With a partner naming the blocks, snaps two or three together and the sprite does one simple action.
levels.2: Snaps command blocks into a stack, including a loop, and the sprite visibly acts when the script is run.
levels.3: Changes the script to make the sprite do something different and explains what each block in it does.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F14

rows.name: Matka decor
steps: Give each child a matka and colours, and show some ideas for lines, shapes and patterns.
Children plan a design on paper with lines, shapes and a repeating pattern.
Decorate the matka by copying the design on to it in colour.
Leave the matkas to dry and then display them.
Children tell a partner which lines, shapes and colours they used.

levels.0: Matka is covered in one colour or scribble, with no clear lines, shapes or repeated pattern visible.
levels.1: After the educator shows a sample pattern, adds lines or shapes in colour but the pattern is not repeated.
levels.2: Decoration on the matka combines lines, shapes and a repeating pattern in several colours.
levels.3: Plans the design on paper first and explains why the colours and patterns were placed where they are.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!G14

rows.name: Sculpture making
steps: Collect clean recycled materials and lay them out for children to choose from.
Children decide what to make and sketch a quick idea.
Make a sculpture by joining the pieces with tape or glue.
Check that the sculpture stands on its own and fix any weak parts.
Children display their sculptures and tell the class what each one is and what it is made of.

levels.0: Pieces of recycled material are stacked loosely or fall apart, and no figure or form can be named.
levels.1: Joining pieces with the educator holding parts steady, builds a rough form from two or three recycled items.
levels.2: Sculpture stands on its own, is made of recycled materials, and can be named as something.
levels.3: Chooses materials for a reason, fixes a weak joint after it wobbles, and explains what the sculpture shows.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!G14

rows.name: Mini Science Observation (once a fortnight)
steps: Choose an object, plant or small creature for the fortnight's observation.
Do a mini science observation: look closely and talk about its colour, shape and size.
Children write what they saw in their own sentences, with a small drawing.
Each child shares one thing they saw with a partner.
Keep the page so it can be compared with the next fortnight's observation.
rows.time_note: Home - Wednesday, from September first week

levels.0: Writing says only a feeling such as 'nice', or copies the name of the thing, with nothing seen described.
levels.1: With a prompt question from the educator such as 'what colour?', writes one thing that was seen.
levels.2: Writes two or more things seen, such as colour, shape or size, in sentences after looking closely.
levels.3: Notes a change between two looks a fortnight apart and says in own words what might have caused it.

rows.note: named in Routines!B14

rows.name: Week 1 – Dancing Poinciana
rows.unit: Unit 3: Poetry – Poems from Different Cultures
steps: Read the poem Dancing Poinciana aloud while children follow the text.
Talk about the vocabulary, including any words children do not know.
Identify the descriptive words and underline them.
Practise reading the poem with expression, in pairs.
A few children read the poem to the class with expression.

levels.0: Reads the poem in a flat, word-by-word way with many stops, and descriptive words are not picked out.
levels.1: Reads aloud with a partner or by echoing the educator, and expression appears only on a few lines.
levels.2: Voice rises and softens on the descriptive words while reading the whole poem aloud smoothly.
levels.3: Chooses a different way to say a line, such as softer or quicker, and explains what the descriptive words picture.

rows.note: Steps follow the educators' planner cell.

rows.name: Week 2 – Hurricane and The Thunder is a Great Dragon
rows.unit: Unit 3: Poetry – Poems from Different Cultures
steps: Read the two poems, Hurricane and The Thunder is a Great Dragon, aloud.
Identify onomatopoeia and list the sound words found.
Talk about what thunder looks and sounds like.
Create a short poem about thunder using sound words.
Read the poem to a partner and share it with the class.

levels.0: Writing is a sentence or list unrelated to thunder, with no line breaks or sound words from the model poems.
levels.1: With the educator giving a first line or sound words, adds one or two lines about thunder.
levels.2: Poem about thunder has several short lines and uses a sound word like those in the model poems.
levels.3: Reads the poem aloud, changes a word to make the sound stronger, and explains the choice.

rows.note: Steps follow the educators' planner cell.

rows.name: Week 3 – Song of the Animal World
rows.unit: Unit 3: Poetry – Poems from Different Cultures
steps: Explore animal and movement vocabulary, repetition and rhythm in Song of the Animal World.
Choose an animal and list words for how it moves and sounds.
Create a verse of your own that includes a repeated line.
Practise performing the verse with voice and actions.
Perform the verse for a partner or the class.

levels.0: Verse is missing or has no animal or movement words, and the performance is mumbled or stops partway.
levels.1: Educator supplies a rhyming or repeating line to copy, and the verse is spoken quietly with the group.
levels.2: Own verse uses animal and movement words with a repeated line, and is performed with voice and actions.
levels.3: Teaches the verse to a partner, adding a new repeated line, and explains how voice and actions show the animal.

rows.note: Steps follow the educators' planner cell.

rows.name: Week 4 – Cat Haiku
rows.unit: Unit 3: Poetry – Poems from Different Cultures
steps: Read Cat Haiku together.
Count the syllables in each line by clapping.
Plan your own haiku on paper, choosing a subject and some words.
Write the haiku in three short lines, counting syllables as you go.
Illustrate the haiku and share it with a partner.

levels.0: Lines are written without counting syllables, so the haiku has long run-on lines and no three-line shape.
levels.1: Claps syllables with a partner and writes one or two lines of the haiku that fit, needing help with the rest.
levels.2: Haiku has three short lines whose syllables fit the model's pattern, with an illustration beside it.
levels.3: Counts and adjusts words to fit syllables in a new haiku on another subject and explains each change.

rows.note: Steps follow the educators' planner cell.

rows.name: Week 5 – Introduction to Myths and Legends
steps: Explore Bear and Fire, Mulan and Sinbad and the Roc by reading them aloud in a group.
Look at the characters, settings and important events of each story.
Begin a simple storyboard of one story in boxes.
Retell the story in your own words by acting it out with the group.
Compare storyboards with a partner and talk about what is the same.

levels.0: Group reading is silent or lost, storyboard boxes are empty or not in order, and the retelling leaves out the main events.
levels.1: Joins the group reading when others lead, draws two or three boxes with educator prompts, and retells with a partner's cues.
levels.2: Takes a turn reading aloud, draws story boxes in order showing characters and setting, and acts out the main events.
levels.3: Acts out the myth with changed voices and explains, in own words, why each storyboard box was chosen.

rows.note: Steps follow the educators' planner cell.

rows.name: Olympiad Mock Test (for Olympiad-registered students)
steps: Arrange the room as for a test and give each Olympiad-registered child the mock paper.
Tell children the time allowed and read the instructions aloud.
Children attempt the Olympiad mock test in the set time.
Call time and ask children to stop writing.
Go over a few questions together and let children say which they found hard.

levels.0: Paper is handed in with most questions blank, or time runs out with only the first few attempted.
levels.1: Reminded of the time by the educator, attempts about half the questions and leaves the rest blank.
levels.2: Attempts every question within the set time, with working or an answer written for each one.
levels.3: Marks own paper afterwards, picks the questions that took longest and explains how to use time differently next time.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C23

rows.name: Hindi: सफ़ाई संबंधी गतिविधि, अभिनय, होर्डिंग पर लिखा संदेश
steps: चित्रकथा 'सजग बच्चे' के चित्र देखें और उन पर बात करें।
Suggested: सफ़ाई से जुड़ी एक छोटी गतिविधि चुनें और उसे जोड़ी में करके दिखाएँ।
जोड़ी बनाकर चित्रकथा के एक भाग का अभिनय करें।
होर्डिंग पर लिखा संदेश पढ़ें/लिखें।
कुछ जोड़ियाँ अपना अभिनय कक्षा के सामने दिखाएँ और बताएँ कि संदेश क्या कहता है।

levels.0: Acting is missing, or only one partner speaks, and the actions do not match the scene in the picture story.
levels.1: Following the educator's cues, acts a few lines and actions, and loses the place without those cues.
levels.2: Acts a part of the picture story with a partner, taking turns, with words and actions that match the picture.
levels.3: Adds new lines to the scene, reads the hoarding message aloud, and explains to the audience what it asks people to do.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D20

rows.name: Hindi: गीत निर्माण, सुनना-सुनाना, चित्र वर्णन
steps: कहानी 'सतरंगी गेंद' के किसी भाग पर गीत बनाएँ।
एक बच्चा गीत सुनाए और बाकी बच्चे ध्यान से सुनें।
सुनने के बाद बताएँ कि कौन-सा चित्र सुने हुए भाग से मेल खाता है।
चित्र का वर्णन करें।
कुछ बच्चे अपना गीत और वर्णन कक्षा में सुनाएँ।

levels.0: Picks a picture that does not match the part heard, or points to pictures without waiting to listen.
levels.1: Picks the matching picture after the part is repeated or the educator narrows the choice to two.
levels.2: Listens to a part of the story or song and points to the one picture that matches it.
levels.3: Says which detail in the picture matches the words heard and describes the picture in own sentences.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D20

rows.name: प्रोजेक्ट – दिमाग लगाओ पहेली सुलझाओ
steps: बच्चों को पहेली दें और उसे ध्यान से पढ़कर सुनाएँ।
Suggested: संकेतों को एक-एक करके पढ़ें और रेखांकित करें।
Suggested: दिमाग लगाएँ और पहेली सुलझाएँ।
Suggested: उत्तर कॉपी में लिखें।
Suggested: साथी को अपना उत्तर बताएँ और यह भी बताएँ कि वह किस संकेत से मिला।

levels.0: Answer is guessed or left blank and does not fit any of the clues given in the puzzle.
levels.1: Reads the clues with an educator and solves part of the puzzle, with a hint needed for the rest.
levels.2: Solves the puzzle with an answer that fits every clue, and can point to the clue behind it.
levels.3: Makes a new puzzle with clues for a partner to solve and explains how the clues lead to the answer.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D20

rows.name: Food Chain chart
steps: Talk about plants and animals and who eats what, using examples children know.
Children choose a plant and some animals for their food chain.
Make a food chain chart: draw or paste each one and join them with arrows pointing from food to eater.
Label each plant and animal by name.
Present the chart to a partner and explain what each arrow means.

levels.0: Chart shows plants and animals without arrows, or arrows point the wrong way, so no feeding order is shown.
levels.1: Educator or partner helps decide who eats whom, and arrows are drawn for one or two links.
levels.2: Food chain on the chart names a plant and animals joined by arrows pointing from food to eater.
levels.3: Builds a second chain in another habitat and explains what happens to the others if one link is removed.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F20

rows.name: Scratch collaborative project: animate a story
steps: Plan a short story in groups and decide the scenes and which sprite is in each.
Open Scratch and choose sprites and backdrops for the story.
Animate the story with a sequence of blocks, giving each sprite its part.
Use event blocks so that sprites move or change when something happens.
Run the project and fix anything that does not work.
Show the animation to another group.

levels.0: Sprites do nothing when the project is run, or react at the wrong time because no event block starts them.
levels.1: With teammates or the educator, adds an event block to one sprite, though the others are not triggered.
levels.2: Sprites in the story move or change their look when an event such as a key press or click happens.
levels.3: Tests the animation with another group, fixes a sprite that reacted late, and explains which event starts each part.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F20

rows.name: Junior chef – sandwich, salad and one sweet dish
steps: Wash hands, clean the work tables and set out the ingredients.
Make a sandwich, step by step.
Make a salad.
Make one sweet dish.
Arrange the foods on a plate.
Talk about what is on the plate and why.

levels.0: Plate holds one kind of food only, or foods are heaped without any grouping.
levels.1: Once food groups are named by the educator, places foods from two groups on the plate.
levels.2: Plate shows foods from several groups, taken from the sandwich, salad and sweet dish, in sensible amounts.
levels.3: Swaps one food to balance a plate that was heavy in one group and explains the swap.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F20

rows.name: Weave old fabrics to make a rug
steps: Cut old fabrics into long strips and gather them with a frame or base to weave on.
Fix the first set of strips in place.
Weave old fabrics to make a rug by passing the other strips over and under.
Push the rows close together and check the pattern.
Finish the edges and show the rug to the class.

levels.0: Strips are laid side by side or stuck flat, with none going over and under.
levels.1: Starting from rows the educator has begun, weaves a few strips over and under before losing the pattern.
levels.2: Weaves strips over and under following the given pattern for the whole rug, with the pattern holding.
levels.3: Creates a new pattern of their own, weaves it, and explains how the over-under order makes it.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F20

rows.name: Killa making (handwork)
steps: Collect clean recycled materials and talk about what a killa looks like.
Plan the killa on paper.
Make a killa from the materials, building walls and a tower or gate.
Check that it stands and strengthen any weak part.
Display the killa and tell the class how it was made.

levels.0: Recycled pieces are not joined into a structure, and no walls or towers of a killa are visible.
levels.1: Walls of the killa stand only while a partner or educator steadies them, and need extra joining.
levels.2: Killa made from recycled materials stands by itself, with walls and at least one tower or gate.
levels.3: Adds features such as steps or a gate after testing strength, and explains how each part was built.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F20

rows.name: Expanded sentences
steps: Write a short sentence on the board.
Ask questions such as what kind, where, when and how to find details to add.
Expand the sentence by adding details.
Children expand their own short sentences in their notebooks.
Read the expanded sentences aloud to a partner.

levels.0: Sentence is copied unchanged, or a word is swapped, with no detail added to it.
levels.1: Adds one detail word after the educator asks 'what kind?' or 'where?'.
levels.2: Rewrites a short sentence with two or more added details, such as how, where or what kind.
levels.3: Expands the same sentence in several ways and explains which details make the picture clearer.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!H23

rows.name: Mental Maths Quiz
steps: Divide the class into teams and explain how the quiz works.
Take part in a mental maths quiz: read each question aloud and ask for answers without writing.
Allow a short time for each answer.
Check the answers and keep score for each team.
Talk about the quick ways children used to get answers.

levels.0: Answers come only after counting on fingers or drawing, or many are incorrect or skipped.
levels.1: Answers some questions quickly when numbers are small, but needs extra time or a hint for others.
levels.2: Gives most answers aloud quickly and correctly without counting aids or writing.
levels.3: Explains the quick method used for an answer and solves a harder question in the same time.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!H23

rows.name: Write an alternative story ending
steps: Read The Abominable Snowman and Yoshi the Stonecutter and talk about how each one ends.
Ask what else might have happened at the end.
Plan a different ending in a few words.
Write an alternative ending.
Read the ending to a partner and compare endings.

levels.0: Writing repeats the original ending, or the ending does not follow from the tale.
levels.1: With a what-if question from the educator, writes one sentence of a different ending.
levels.2: Writes a different ending that follows on from the tale and differs from the original.
levels.3: Compares the new ending with the original and explains how the characters' fate changes.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B24

rows.name: Write a circular story
steps: Talk about stories that end where they began.
Plan a circular story by deciding on the opening and how the ending will return to it.
Write a circular story.
Read the beginning and ending to a partner to check they match up.
Share a few circular stories with the class.

levels.0: Story ends somewhere new, with the opening scene or sentence never coming back.
levels.1: Only after being shown the opening line does the ending echo it.
levels.2: Story's final lines return to the opening event or sentence, so it loops back to the start.
levels.3: Tells the circular story aloud and explains in own words why the ending leads back to the beginning.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B24

rows.name: Perform in character
steps: Listen carefully to character voice as the educator reads part of a story.
Talk about how the voice changes for different characters.
Perform in character using the voice in different ways.
Talk about the sequence of the story.
Watch other groups and say which voice suited each character.

levels.0: Performance uses one flat voice throughout, and the order of events is jumbled or missing.
levels.1: Cues from a partner help the character's voice change a little, and the events come in order with pauses.
levels.2: Acts out the story in a character voice, changing it for different moments, with events in order.
levels.3: Switches characters in a retelling, with a distinct voice for each, and says why the voice changes.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B24

rows.name: Hindi: कविता चार्ट पेपर पर लिखना, चित्र निर्माण (जाड़े की धूप)
steps: कविता 'जाड़े की धूप' पढ़ें।
कविता को चार्ट पेपर पर लिखें।
चित्र बनाएँ।
जाड़े की धूप के बारे में अपनी कुछ पंक्तियाँ लिखें।
चार्ट कक्षा में दिखाएँ और कविता सुनाएँ।

levels.0: Chart holds a copied poem or a few words, with no lines of their own about winter sunshine.
levels.1: With the educator's first line, adds one or two lines about sunshine in winter and a drawing.
levels.2: Writes a short poem of their own on the chart paper about winter sunshine, with a matching picture.
levels.3: Poem uses a comparison or a feeling about the warmth of the sun and is read aloud with expression.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D24

rows.name: Hindi: विचार-अभिव्यक्ति, कहानी-पठन, अनुच्छेद-लेखन (अब हम दोस्त हैं)
steps: बच्चे दोस्ती के बारे में अपने विचार व्यक्त करें।
कहानी 'अब हम दोस्त हैं' पढ़ें और सुनाएँ।
कहानी के बारे में साथी से बात करें।
अनुच्छेद-लेखन करें।
अनुच्छेद पढ़कर सुनाएँ।

levels.0: Paragraph is one or two disconnected words or sentences copied from the book, with no ideas of their own on friendship.
levels.1: After talking with a partner, writes one or two sentences about friendship, needing help to join them into a paragraph.
levels.2: Writes a paragraph of several sentences in own words about the story and about friendship.
levels.3: Paragraph links the story to a real friendship, giving a reason, and is read out to the group.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D24

rows.name: Hindi: अनुच्छेद-लेखन, सूची-निर्माण, रंग भरकर रंगों के नाम (जैसी हूँ मैं)
steps: कहानी 'जैसी हूँ मैं अच्छी हूँ' पढ़ें।
अनुच्छेद लिखें।
सूची बनाएँ।
रंग भरकर रंगों के नाम लिखें।
साथी को अपना लिखा सुनाएँ।

levels.0: Coloured picture has labels only, or copied sentences, and nothing of their own about it.
levels.1: Asked 'what do you see?' by the educator, writes one sentence about the picture.
levels.2: Sentences of own about the coloured picture appear, using colour names written in Hindi.
levels.3: Describes the picture with a reason for the colours chosen and reads the paragraph to a partner.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D24

rows.name: Paper strip weaving
steps: Gather the materials and set out the workspace.
Weave paper strips over and under to make a woven mat.
Show the finished work to a partner and say what was done.
rows.materials: Paper strips (ready-made strips or patterns may be given for support)

levels.0: Strips lie side by side, and none goes over and under another.
levels.1: Mat shows over-under for one row, and other rows need the educator's hand to guide.
levels.2: Mat shows strips going over one and under one in every row, matching the given pattern.
levels.3: Paper strip weaving: the child weaves a new pattern and explains the over-under rule aloud to a friend.

rows.name: Klee-inspired cityscape or Kusama polka-dot art
steps: View and discuss selected art by Paul Klee or Yayoi Kusama.
Make a Klee-inspired cityscape or Kusama-style polka-dot art.
Show the finished work to a partner and say what was made.
rows.materials: Not listed in the document (pictures of the artist's work, art materials)

levels.0: Own artwork has no lines or patterns from the artist's work, and the artist is not named.
levels.1: Art uses dots or boxes like the artist after a prompt, and one line or pattern is named.
levels.2: Cityscape or dot art repeats the artist's lines or polka dots, and the child names one line and one pattern seen.
levels.3: Klee-inspired cityscape or Kusama: the child compares the two artists' lines or patterns aloud and uses that idea in a new piece.

rows.note: named in G2-G3 Visual Arts Curriculum!Week 6: Artist Week – Line & Pattern; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Doodle & Describe
steps: Give each child a blank page and a couple of minutes to doodle freely.
Children look at their doodle and think of words for its shapes, lines and colours.
Each child writes sentences of their own describing the doodle.
Partners swap pages; the reader points to each part of the doodle the sentences describe.
A few children read their description aloud and the class guesses what the doodle looks like.
rows.time_note: Home - Tuesday, once a fortnight, from November third week

levels.0: Doodle has only a title or single words beside it, with no complete sentence describing what is drawn.
levels.1: With an educator asking 'What do you see?' and helping to sound out words, one sentence about the doodle is written.
levels.2: Writes two or more complete sentences in own words that match features of the doodle, with capital letters and full stops.
levels.3: Writes sentences with added detail such as position, size or number, and a partner can find each described feature in the doodle.

rows.note: named in Routines!B13

rows.name: Expanded Sentences
steps: Write a short sentence on the board and read it aloud with the class.
Ask who, what kind, where and when questions, and add the answers to the sentence one detail at a time.
In pairs, children expand a short sentence orally.
Each child writes their own short sentence, then writes it again with at least two added details.
Read the short and expanded versions aloud and compare how they differ.

levels.0: Rewrites the short sentence unchanged or adds only an unrelated word, so the sentence stays the same length.
levels.1: Adds one detail, such as a colour or a place, only after the educator asks 'Where?' or 'What kind?'.
levels.2: Expands a short sentence alone by adding two or more details, such as describing words and where or when, that still read correctly.
levels.3: Builds the same sentence up in several steps with growing detail, and tells a partner what each added word tells the reader.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!I24

rows.name: Short Essay + Drawing
steps: Choose a familiar topic with the class and talk about it for a few minutes.
Each child draws a picture of the topic and jots down three ideas in the order they want to write them.
Children write a short essay with an opening idea, a middle idea and a closing idea.
Partners read each other's essays and check that the ideas follow the order of the drawing.
Display the essays with their drawings and let children read one aloud.

levels.0: Sentences jump between ideas or repeat one idea, with no clear first, next or last point in the essay.
levels.1: Using a planning frame with first, next and last boxes, ideas sit in order but one part is thin or missing.
levels.2: Short essay has an opening idea, one or two middle ideas and a closing idea in a sensible order matching the drawing.
levels.3: Uses linking words such as first, then and finally, and explains to a partner why the ideas were placed in that order.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!I24

rows.name: Design a robot with labels
steps: Read about robots (The Pepper robot, What is a Drone?, Flying a drone) and talk about what each one can do.
Children draw a large design of their own robot on paper.
Add labels with lines pointing to the robot's parts, saying what each part does.
Write short headings and sentences that sort the information about the robot under each heading.
Partners read each other's design and say what the robot looks like and can do.

levels.0: Drawing shows a robot with no labels or headings, or labels sit in one unsorted list under no heading.
levels.1: Given a heading idea by the educator, writes one heading with a sentence or labels under it, leaving other parts unsorted.
levels.2: Writes information about their own robot under two or more clear headings, with labelled parts that match the drawing.
levels.3: Chooses own headings that fit the information and adds facts from the robot reading, explaining why each heading was chosen.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B33

rows.name: Write instructions for a robot
steps: Look at an example set of instructions and underline the first word of each step, talking about command words such as 'walk' and 'turn'.
Choose a simple task for a robot to do.
Children write numbered steps for the robot, starting each step with a command verb.
A partner acts as the robot and follows the steps exactly as written.
Children fix any step that did not work and read the final instructions to the class.

levels.0: Steps begin with words like 'The robot' or 'Then', so no step opens with a command verb such as 'walk' or 'turn'.
levels.1: Reminded to start with an action word, two or three steps open with command verbs while other steps do not.
levels.2: Every step in the numbered set starts with a command verb and the steps run in a workable order.
levels.3: Revises steps after a partner acting as the robot follows them exactly, keeping a precise command verb at the start of each.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B33

rows.name: Write a robot explanation text
steps: Recap what the class learned about robots and list key facts on the board.
Each child chooses a robot and decides on two or three headings for their text.
Children write an explanation under each heading about what the robot is, how it works or what it is for.
Partners find each heading in the text and say whether the sentences below it fit.
Share a few explanation texts with the class.

levels.0: Explanation runs as one block of text with no headings, or headings are present but the sentences below do not match them.
levels.1: Supplied with heading ideas by the educator, writes sentences under one heading while the rest stays a single run of text.
levels.2: Explanation about a robot is split by two or more headings, and the sentences under each heading match it.
levels.3: Adds an extra heading of their own and fits new facts beneath it, so a partner can find any fact quickly using the headings.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B33

rows.name: Present ideas about a robot
steps: Each child prepares a few notes or a picture about a robot.
Children practise saying their ideas to a partner.
In small groups, each child presents their ideas about a robot, using the notes or picture.
Group members listen to the ideas of others and each listener says one thing they learned.
Educator notes whether each presenter was heard clearly and used the notes or picture.

levels.0: Stands before the group but reads notes silently or says nothing, so the group hears no ideas about the robot.
levels.1: Standing beside an educator or partner who prompts each point, shares one or two ideas in a quiet voice from the notes.
levels.2: Speaks to the group for several sentences about the robot, pointing to notes or picture, and each idea is audible.
levels.3: Answers a listener's question about the robot and adds an idea that is not on the notes, linking it to the picture.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B33

rows.name: Perform a poem in a group
steps: Read the poem the group has chosen from Busy Day, Downhill Racer or The River.
Each group decides who reads which lines and where all voices join.
Practise the poem, deciding which words to say loudly, softly, quickly or slowly.
Groups perform the poem for the class while the others listen to the reading aloud.
After each performance, children say in the group what they liked and give an opinion on what to change.

levels.0: Poem is read in an even, flat voice, with lines run together and no change in volume or pace.
levels.1: Reciting alongside a partner or with educator cues, voice changes on one or two lines while other lines stay flat.
levels.2: Recites the poem with clear changes in loudness or speed that match the words, and joins the group on time.
levels.3: Gives reasons for chosen voice changes, such as soft for a calm line, and recites with changes that fit each part.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B33

rows.name: Write a shape poem
steps: Read a model poem together and notice the rhyming words.
Each child chooses a shape and lists words that describe it.
Find rhyming word pairs from the list.
Write the poem so that the lines are arranged in the chosen shape.
Read the shape poem aloud to a partner, who points out the rhymes.

levels.0: Lines are written without rhyming pairs, or the poem copies the model line for line with no new words.
levels.1: Following the model line by line with educator help, one rhyming pair appears while other lines do not rhyme.
levels.2: Short poem written in the chosen shape has at least two rhyming pairs and follows the pattern of the model.
levels.3: Poem on a self-chosen shape uses rhymes not found in the model, and is read aloud with the rhyming words stressed.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B33

rows.name: Write a poem with a repeating pattern
steps: Read a model poem that has a repeating line or pattern and clap the repeat together.
Each child chooses a topic and a line to repeat.
Write the poem using the repeated line and new lines that rhyme.
Read the poems aloud while the class joins in on the repeating line.
Partners check that the repeating line appears in each place it should.

levels.0: Poem lines are all different, with no repeated line or rhyme appearing anywhere in the writing.
levels.1: Using a sentence starter from the educator, repeats a line twice, but the new lines do not rhyme.
levels.2: Poem repeats a chosen line at set places and has rhyming words in at least two of the new lines.
levels.3: Changes the repeating line slightly to fit each verse while keeping rhymes, and says in own words what the repeat adds.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B33

rows.name: Find the centre of a circle by folding
steps: Give each child a paper circle and show how to fold it in half and in half again.
Open the circle; the crease lines meet at the centre, which children mark.
Draw a pointer arrow from the centre, then call out a quarter turn, half turn or full turn for children to turn the pointer using the folds.
In pairs, one child calls a turn and the other turns the pointer and checks it against the creases.
Share which turns were easy and how the folds helped.

levels.0: Pointer turns by an arbitrary amount, so it does not stop on the fold lines for a quarter, half or full turn.
levels.1: Turns correctly for a half or full turn but needs the educator to show the quarter turn along the folds.
levels.2: Pointer turns through a quarter, half and full turn as called, stopping on the matching crease each time.
levels.3: Predicts where the pointer will stop for a new turn, such as two quarter turns one after the other, and shows it with the folds.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!C33

rows.name: Chance Game: spinner colours
steps: Look at a spinner with different colours.
Guess which colour it will land on.
Spin it several times and record each result.
Say which colour came up most.

levels.0: Says the spinner 'must' land on red and does not change the guess after it lands on blue.
levels.1: Records spin results only with the educator reading the spinner colour each time.
levels.2: Records results of several spins and says which colour is more likely, using 'likely' or 'maybe'.
levels.3: Predicts a new spinner's likely colour from its picture and explains using results from the spins.

rows.name: Project: 100 Squares
steps: Give each child a hundred square grid to use for the 100 Squares project.
Children choose a number pattern and mark it on the grid.
Write the first few terms of the pattern, then continue it for three more terms.
A partner checks the new terms by looking at the marked squares.
Share what the class noticed about the patterns on the grid.

levels.0: Next numbers written after the given terms do not follow the step between them, jumping by differing amounts.
levels.1: Pointing along the hundred square or helped by a partner's hint, continues the pattern for one or two terms only.
levels.2: Writes three more terms after the first few given, each following the same step, and marks them on the grid.
levels.3: Names the rule of the pattern in own words and continues it past three terms, or creates a new pattern for a partner.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!C33

rows.name: Hindi: होली की कहानी, चित्र में रंग भरना, शब्द-पहेली, कविता-लेखन
steps: होली की कहानी पढ़ें।
कहानी के बारे में बात करें कि उसमें क्या-क्या हुआ।
चित्र में रंग भरें।
शब्द-पहेली हल करें।
कहानी से जुड़े प्रश्नों के उत्तर पूरे वाक्यों में लिखें।
कविता-लेखन करें और एक-दो बच्चे अपनी रचना पढ़कर सुनाएँ।

levels.0: Answers to Holi story questions are single words or copied phrases, with no complete sentence written.
levels.1: Hearing each question read aloud and given the first word by the educator, writes some answers as full sentences.
levels.2: Writes answers to the story questions in full Hindi sentences of their own, each with a verb and ending in '।'.
levels.3: Answers go beyond the text, adding a reason or an opinion about the Holi story, still in full sentences.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D33

rows.name: Hindi: श्रुतलेखन (dictation)
steps: बच्चे कॉपी और पेंसिल निकालकर तैयार हों।
एक वाक्य दो बार धीरे-धीरे बोलें।
श्रुतलेखन करें: बच्चे सुनकर वाक्य अपनी कॉपी में लिखें।
बच्चे साथी से कॉपी बदलकर वाक्य की वर्तनी जाँचें।
गलत लिखे शब्दों को सही वर्तनी में दोबारा लिखें।

levels.0: Dictated sentence has several words with missing or wrong matras ('मात्रा'), so many words cannot be read as dictated.
levels.1: After the sentence is repeated word by word, most words are written, though two or three show wrong matras.
levels.2: Dictated sentence is written with every word spelt correctly, including matras, and ends with '।'.
levels.3: Writes a longer dictated sentence correctly and corrects a partner's misspelt word, saying which matra was wrong.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D33

rows.name: Input/Output Hunt: create simple micro:bit programs
steps: Join the Input/Output Hunt: find the inputs and the outputs on the micro:bit.
Create a simple program so that pressing an input makes an output happen, such as a pattern on the LEDs.
Run it on the micro:bit and fill in the micro:bit project sheet.

levels.0: Program blocks are not joined to a button event, so the LEDs show nothing when the button is pressed.
levels.1: Gets a pattern to show on the LEDs only after the educator helps to connect the button block.
levels.2: Button press on the micro:bit lights the LED pattern chosen, with the project sheet naming input and output.
levels.3: Changes the pattern and the button used, then tells a partner which block caused each change.

rows.name: Preservatives: making pickles and papads
steps: Talk about natural and artificial preservatives, and let children share foods they know that keep for a long time.
Wash hands and set out the materials for pickles and papads.
Make pickles and papads in groups, noting what is done to help them keep.
Children say why they think the pickles and papads will not spoil quickly.
Each child names one way to keep food from spoiling.

levels.0: Answers about keeping food fresh name no method, saying only that food 'goes bad' without naming how to stop it.
levels.1: Seeing the pickles and papads, names one ingredient or step used in making them once the educator points to it.
levels.2: Names at least one way to keep food from spoiling, such as a preservative used in the pickles or papads.
levels.3: Names two ways, sorting them as natural or artificial, and says in own words why preserved food lasts longer.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!E37

rows.name: Make a cardboard loom
steps: Gather the materials and set out the workspace.
Make a cardboard loom with strings stretched across it.
Show the finished work to a partner and say what was done.

levels.0: Loom strings hang slack or tangled, so no weaving can begin.
levels.1: Loom is strung with help from the educator in fixing the first strings.
levels.2: Cardboard loom holds straight, tight strings side by side, ready for weaving.
levels.3: Weaves one row over and under on the loom and explains why the strings must stay tight.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 & 3 - Stitching and Weaving Science Curriculum!Fortnight 7 & 8: Types of Weaving Techniques (Activities); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Republic Day song practice
steps: Gather the class and listen to the Republic Day song once.
Practise the song line by line, with children echoing each line.
Sing the whole song together at a steady pace.
Small groups take turns singing the song for the others.
Children say which part they sing best and which part to practise more.

levels.0: Mouths or hums only, or sings lines with words and tune out of step with the group.
levels.1: Joins in on the chorus or some lines when the educator leads, and drops out between them.
levels.2: Sings the song's words along with the group from start to end, keeping to the same tune and pace.
levels.3: Sings with steady tune and clear words, and leads a line or helps others keep time when asked.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!G33

rows.name: Weigh It!
steps: Choose classroom objects to weigh.
Guess each mass before weighing.
Weigh each object on the scale and write its mass.
Compare your guess with the measured mass.

levels.0: Writes a mass of 5 kg for a pencil and keeps it after it is weighed on the scale.
levels.1: Reads the scale only when the educator points to the needle and says which units it shows.
levels.2: Estimates the mass of an object, weighs it on the scale and writes both numbers.
levels.3: Estimates a heavier object in kilograms, checks it, and explains how the earlier guesses helped.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!12. Measures: Mass, Capacity, Temperature – Period 1; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Grain to Flour: from wheat to ladoo
steps: Find out where flour comes from by looking at wheat grains together.
Experience the traditional method of making flour, with the educator handling anything unsafe.
Sort real or pictured foods into grains and pulses.
Make ladoo together in groups.
Children say which foods in the day's work were grains and which were pulses.

levels.0: Foods are placed in mixed groups, with grains and pulses side by side and no stated reason for the grouping.
levels.1: Sorts a few samples correctly after the educator names one grain and one pulse as examples, leaving others misplaced.
levels.2: Sorts real or pictured foods into grains and pulses, with wheat among the grains, and no more than one misplaced.
levels.3: Adds a food of their own to each group after sorting every sample, and says how a grain differs from a pulse.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F28

rows.name: Design a snowman with socks and buttons
steps: Look at the socks and buttons and talk about what a snowman needs.
Each child draws a plan to design their snowman.
Shape the snowman's body from a sock.
Attach the buttons and other parts using the stitching technique taught.
Show the finished snowman and compare it with the plan.

levels.0: Snowman is left as a sock with buttons loose or stuck on, with no stitches holding any part.
levels.1: Threading help from an educator gets one or two buttons stitched on, and the product stays unfinished.
levels.2: Finished snowman has buttons attached with stitches and the sock shaped as designed, matching the plan drawing.
levels.3: Finished snowman adds own sewn features, and the maker names the stitch used and what could improve.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F28

rows.name: Colour wheel on paper plates
steps: Mix red, yellow and blue to create secondary colours.
Make a simple colour wheel on paper plates.
Show the finished work to a partner and say what was made.
rows.materials: Not listed in the document (red, yellow, blue paint, paper plates)

levels.0: Plate wheel has muddy or missing secondary colours, or primaries and secondaries are in the wrong places.
levels.1: Wheel shows orange, green and purple after the educator reminds which two colours to mix for each.
levels.2: Plate wheel shows red, yellow and blue with orange, green and purple between the right neighbours, and the child names them.
levels.3: Mixes a requested new colour from two primaries on a fresh plate and explains the mix aloud.

rows.note: named in G2-G3 Visual Arts Curriculum!Week 7: Colour Wheel; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Hindi: भालू का घर – कहानी का अंत बदलना, पशु-पक्षियों के घर
steps: कहानी-वाचन करें।
कहानी के अंत के बारे में बात करें कि अंत में क्या हुआ।
कहानी का अंत बदलें: बच्चे नया अंत सोचें।
नया अंत अपने वाक्यों में लिखें।
(cell topic only; suggested) हर पशु-पक्षी के चित्र को उसके घर (घोंसला, बिल, माँद) से जोड़ें।
साथी को अपना नया अंत पढ़कर सुनाएँ।

levels.0: New ending repeats the original ending word for word, or only one word or phrase is written.
levels.1: After talking through a new ending with the educator, writes one sentence for it, in words close to the story's.
levels.2: Writes a different ending of two or more sentences in own words that still fits what happened in the story.
levels.3: Gives a reason in own words for why the new ending changes what happens, alongside the written ending.

rows.name: Write an ending to a given story
steps: Read the given story together and stop before the ending.
Talk about how it could end and what might happen next.
Each child plans a new ending in a few words.
Children write the ending to the story in their own sentences.
Read the ending aloud to a partner and compare how the endings differ.

levels.0: Ending is left blank, or retells the story's own ending in the same words with nothing new.
levels.1: Following the educator's 'What if...?' question, writes a one-sentence different ending not connected to earlier events.
levels.2: Writes an ending different from the original that follows from earlier events, in at least two sentences.
levels.3: Compares own ending with the original, saying what changes for the characters, and the ending keeps the tale's style.
