rows.name: Write a short animal story with a beginning, middle and end
steps: Talk about animals and choose one for a story, with a problem it could face.
Fold paper into three parts for the beginning, middle and end, and jot ideas in each.
Write a short animal story with a clear beginning, middle and end.
Read the story to a partner, who points to where each part starts.
Share a few stories with the class.

levels.0: Story is a single event or list of facts about an animal, with no separate beginning, middle and end.
levels.1: With a three-part folded plan from the educator, two parts are written, usually beginning and middle, with no clear end.
levels.2: Animal story has a clear beginning that introduces the animal, a middle event, and an ending that closes it.
levels.3: Story's ending resolves the problem set up in the beginning, and the writer points out each part to a partner.

rows.name: Project – Sorting Orange Juice
steps: Introduce the Sorting Orange Juice project and read its problem together.
Children underline the numbers and what is being asked.
Children work out the problem in two steps, writing each step as a number sentence.
Check the answer by reading it back against the problem.
Pairs explain their two steps to another pair.

levels.0: Work shows one number operation that answers only part of the problem, and the final answer does not address the question asked.
levels.1: Guided by the educator splitting the problem into parts, the first step is worked correctly but the second is missing or mistaken.
levels.2: Two steps are written as number sentences in the right order, and the final answer is labelled and fits the situation.
levels.3: Explains why each step is needed, checks the answer against the story, and makes up a similar two-step problem.

rows.name: Hindi: पौधारोपण गतिविधि, सूचना-लेखन, जानवरों के नाम
steps: पौधारोपण करें।
पौधा लगाते समय बात करें कि प्रकृति को बचाने के लिए हम क्या कर सकते हैं।
सूचना-लेखन करें: प्रकृति की रक्षा के बारे में छोटी सूचना अपने वाक्यों में लिखें।
जानवरों के नाम बताएँ।
साथी को अपनी सूचना पढ़कर सुनाएँ।

levels.0: Writing is a list of words or a copied line, with no notice heading 'सूचना' and no message about nature.
levels.1: Copying a model notice and using the educator's sentence starter, writes a heading and one sentence about caring for nature.
levels.2: Notice has a heading 'सूचना' and two or more sentences in own words telling others how to protect nature.
levels.3: Notice gives a reason for protecting nature and a clear request to readers, all in own sentences.

rows.name: Hindi: होली के रंग – कविता-लेखन
steps: होली की कहानी पढ़ें।
कहानी के बारे में बात करें कि उसमें क्या-क्या हुआ।
कहानी से जुड़े प्रश्नों के उत्तर पूरे वाक्यों में लिखें।
कविता-लेखन करें: होली पर अपनी कविता लिखें।

levels.0: Lines about Holi are single words or phrases, so no sentence in the notebook answers a question about the story.
levels.1: When the educator asks each question aloud and a partner helps, one sentence about the story is written.
levels.2: Notebook answers on the Holi story are full sentences, and poem lines reuse events or words from the story.
levels.3: Poem lines and answers together show own ideas beyond the text, such as feelings about the festival, in complete sentences.

rows.name: Light experiment project
steps: Set up a place that is dim enough for a light source to show clearly.
Each group chooses an object and places it between the light source and a wall or sheet of paper.
Children make a shadow with the object and observe it.
Draw the shadow and write or say what is needed to make it.
Share the drawings and talk about what changed the shadow.

levels.0: Light source is switched on but the object is not between it and the surface, so no shadow appears.
levels.1: Held steady by an educator, the light source casts a shadow of the object, and the maker points to it.
levels.2: Object placed in the light's path makes a clear shadow on a surface, which is pointed out and named.
levels.3: Moves the object or light to change the shadow's size or position, and says what was changed and what happened.

Program the micro:bit so that pressing an input shows the pattern on the LEDs.
Test the program with the drawn bedroom and fix any problems.
Show the Smart Bedroom to the group and say what the pattern means.

levels.0: Smart bedroom plan lists ideas, but the micro:bit shows nothing, or a pattern shows without any press.
levels.1: Once a partner finds the input block, the bedroom feature shows an LED pattern for a button, though it sometimes fails.

Talk about texture, colour, smell and taste before and after baking.

levels.0: Remarks describe the dough only, with no cooking method named and no change after heating mentioned.
levels.1: When asked by the educator, names the cooking method but describes the change with one vague word.
levels.2: Names baking or the method used and states one change seen, such as in texture or colour.
levels.3: Compares before and after on texture, colour, smell and taste, and links each change to the heat of cooking.

rows.name: Steam in a pan
steps: Heat water in a pan with only the educator handling the heat, while children stand back.
Observe the water turning into steam.
Explain that steam is hot water vapour.
Discuss safety rules while observing steam.
Relate steam to daily life, such as cooking rice, vegetables and idlis, and let each child name a food cooked with steam.

levels.0: Statements about the pan mention only the water or noise, with no steam, cooking method or effect on food named.
levels.1: Prompted by the educator's picture of idlis or rice, names steaming but says little about what steam does.
levels.2: Names steaming as a cooking method and says that steam, hot water vapour, cooks food such as rice or idlis.
levels.3: Describes the water changing to steam in the pan, links it to steaming food, and states one safety rule.

rows.name: Nail string art
steps: Before the lesson, fix nails in a simple outline on a board so each child or pair has a surface to wrap around.
Show how to tie a string to one nail and wrap it round other nails to make straight lines.
Children create patterns by wrapping colourful strings around nails, changing to a second colour at least once.
Children show their pattern to a partner and name the shape and colours they used.

levels.0: Wrapping stays on one nail or tangles, so no clear design shows and only a single colour of string is used.
levels.1: Once the educator ties the first knot, a design appears in two colours but gaps remain between wraps.
levels.2: Strings wrapped nail to nail form a recognisable star, flower or letter shape using two or more colours.
levels.3: Designs a new shape on the nails unprompted, changes colours deliberately, and explains why each colour sits where it does.

steps: Observe texture photos (fur, woodgrain, pebbles).
Create black-and-white texture swatches using pencil.
Show the finished work to a partner and say what was made.

levels.0: Swatch is a flat grey patch, and the lines do not look like the photographed surface.
levels.1: Swatch shows one kind of line for fur after the educator suggests short lines.
levels.2: Swatches for fur, woodgrain and pebbles each use different lines and shading that look like the photo.
levels.3: Visual texture swatches: the child draws a swatch of a new surface from a photo and says which lines and shading suit it.

levels.1: Jungle has a background and one added leaf layer once the educator shows where to stack leaves.
levels.2: Jungle shows a painted background with leaves and animals layered in front, and the child points out each layer.

rows.name: Write structured paragraphs
steps: Choose an underwater topic from the unit and gather a few facts about it on the board with the class.
Show a frame of topic sentence, details and conclusion, and model one paragraph on the board with a heading.
Children write paragraphs with a topic sentence, details and conclusion on a topic they pick, adding a heading.
Partners read each other's paragraph and tick the topic sentence, the details and the conclusion.

levels.0: Writing is a list of loose sentences with no opening statement, closing line or heading.
levels.1: Using the educator's sentence frame, a topic sentence and one or two details appear, but ending and heading are missing.
levels.2: Paragraph under a heading opens with a topic sentence, adds details about the same topic, and ends with a concluding line.
levels.3: Writes a paragraph on a fresh topic with its own heading and explains what each of the three parts does.

rows.name: Create information charts (2–3 columns)
steps: Collect facts about underwater life on the board as children call them out.
Draw a chart with 2 or 3 columns on the board and show how each column gets a heading.
Children create an information chart with 2–3 columns, writing facts under the right heading.
Partners swap charts and check that each fact sits under the heading it belongs to.

levels.0: Facts are scattered across the page with no column lines or headings, or one heading is used for everything.
levels.1: Given a ruled template, headings are copied in and a few facts fill one or two columns.
levels.2: A chart of two or three columns, each with a heading, holds facts that match the heading above them.
levels.3: Plans own column headings for a new topic and fills the chart, then explains why each fact belongs in its column.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B45

rows.name: Explain food chains orally; share coral reef facts
steps: Give children time to prepare a picture or a few notes about a food chain or a coral reef fact.
In the circle, children explain food chains orally, pointing to their picture or notes.
Children share coral reef facts with the group.
Take part in guided report discussions, with the educator asking a question and a listener asking one too.

levels.0: Speaks only a word or two, or stays silent, and the group cannot tell what was found out.
levels.1: Prompts such as 'what eats what?' lead to one food chain link, read from the notes.
levels.2: Presents a food chain or reef fact to the group in connected sentences, glancing at notes or pointing to a picture.
levels.3: Presents clearly without reading, answers a listener's question, and adds a fact that is not on the notes.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B45

rows.name: Write rhyming verses, a short ode and a class poem
steps: Read a short rhyming model poem aloud and have children spot and underline the rhyming words.
Children list rhyming pairs for a creature of their choice and write rhyming verses.
Children compose a short ode of 2–3 stanzas using their rhyming pairs.
Each child contributes a line to a class poem, and the class reads the finished poem aloud together.

levels.0: Lines are written without end rhyme, or copy the model line for line.
levels.1: Helped by a rhyme word list, one rhyming pair appears but the other lines do not match.
levels.2: Short poem following the model has line endings that rhyme in each verse, in the shape of the model.
levels.3: Poem on own creature uses fresh rhyming pairs not found in the model, and the poet says how the rhymes were found.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B45

rows.name: Recite poems clearly and confidently
steps: Choose a poem and read it aloud once as a model, using your voice and face to show feeling.
Children recite the poem clearly in pairs, with the partner listening for words that are hard to hear.
Practise projection and pacing by reciting to the far side of the room and pausing at line ends.
Children express emotion through voice and facial expression as each recites to the class, and listeners name one thing done well.

levels.0: Poem is mumbled or read in one flat tone, with words skipped and little change in face.
levels.1: Echoing the educator line by line, words are clear but expression changes in only a line or two.
levels.2: Poem is said audibly at an even pace, with voice and face matching the feeling of the lines.
levels.3: Recites from memory with deliberate pauses and varied voice, and says which feeling a line was given and how the voice showed it.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!B45

rows.name: Project: Possibly odd
steps: Open the project 'Possibly odd' (unit 1) and read what it asks together so every child knows the task.
Give children the numbers or materials the project uses, and have them sort numbers up to 100 into odd and even.
Children record their sorted numbers and write how they decided where each one goes.
Partners compare their lists and talk about any number they placed differently.

levels.0: Numbers are placed in odd and even groups with no pattern, or the ones digit is not used.
levels.1: Pairing counters or following a hint, a few numbers are sorted correctly while larger ones are misplaced.
levels.2: Numbers up to 100 are sorted into odd and even lists, with the ones digit named as the reason.
levels.3: Predicts whether a number chosen by a partner is odd or even and justifies it using its ones digit.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!C45

rows.name: Project: Strange submarines
steps: Open the project 'Strange submarines' (unit 3) and read the task aloud with the class.
Ask children to say in their own words what the problem asks before they start.
Children work through the project, writing each step of the working on paper.
Pairs compare working and answers and explain how each step led to the next.

levels.0: Working shows one operation only, or numbers from the problem are combined without reading what is asked.
levels.1: Reading the problem aloud with the educator, one step is worked and the second is left.
levels.2: Both steps of the submarine problem are written as number sentences and the final answer fits the question.
levels.3: Makes up an own two-step problem on a similar theme and explains how each step leads to the answer.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!C45

rows.name: Project: Pencil swap
steps: Open the project 'Pencil swap' (unit 5) and read the task aloud with the class.
Ask children to say in their own words what the problem asks before they start.
Children work through the project, writing each step of the working on paper.
Pairs compare working and answers and explain how each step led to the next.

levels.0: Answer is a single number with no steps visible, and it does not match what the pencil problem asks.
levels.1: After a partner re-reads the problem, one calculation is shown and the second step is unfinished.
levels.2: Two linked calculations appear in the working, and the answer is written as a sentence that answers the question.
levels.3: Changes the numbers or story of the pencil problem and solves the new two-step version, explaining the order of steps.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!C45

rows.name: Project: Time a task
steps: Open the project 'Time a task' (unit 4) and read what it asks together.
Choose a short classroom task, and have children note the start time from a clock before beginning.
Children do the task, note the end time, and work out how long it took.
Children share their start time, end time and length with a partner and check each other's working.

levels.0: Start and end times are recorded but the elapsed time is missing or equals one of those times.
levels.1: Aided by a clock face from the educator, elapsed time is found for whole hours only.
levels.2: Start and end times are noted for the task, and the length is worked out correctly in minutes or hours.
levels.3: Times a second, different task, compares the two lengths and explains how the answer was found from the clock.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!C45

rows.name: Project: 100 square
steps: Open the project '100 square' (unit 10) and give each child a hundred square.
Show a number pattern on the square with the first few terms marked, and ask what comes next.
Children continue the pattern on their square for three more terms, colouring each one.
Partners check each other's pattern and say the rule they followed.

levels.0: Coloured or marked squares show no regular rule, and the pattern is not extended.
levels.1: When the educator names the jump size, two more numbers are added before the pattern breaks.
levels.2: Three more numbers continue the pattern from the first few given on the hundred square, following the same jump.
levels.3: Spots and states the rule on the grid and creates a new pattern on a hundred square with a different jump.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!C45

rows.name: Making circuits
steps: Ask children to find where we use electricity at home and at school, and list their ideas on the board.
Show a battery, a bulb and wires, and show how to handle them safely.
In small groups, children make circuits by connecting the battery, bulb and wires until the bulb lights.
Children draw the circuit that worked and tell the class what they changed to make it light.

levels.0: Bulb stays unlit because wires touch only one end of the battery or bulb, and the attempt is left there.
levels.1: Guided to the battery ends, the bulb lights with partner help but the arrangement cannot be repeated.
levels.2: Battery, bulb and wires are joined in a loop so the bulb lights, and the arrangement can be rebuilt on request.
levels.3: Explains in own words why the bulb goes out when one wire is lifted, and lights it again using a new arrangement.

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!F45

rows.name: Samaaroh project: stitched decor
steps: Recall the stitching techniques taught so far and show samples of each.
In groups, decide what decor to make for the Samaaroh event and sketch it with a colour plan.
Children use stitching techniques to create the decor, with each child stitching a part.
Display the finished decor and let each group say which techniques they used.

levels.0: Stitching is begun but only loose practice stitches exist, with no finished decor item.
levels.1: Stitched in parts with educator help threading and knotting, the decor item is left unfinished or uneven.
levels.2: A finished decor item for the event shows the stitching or weaving techniques taught in class.
levels.3: Finished decor combines more than one technique with a planned colour scheme, and the maker explains the choices for the event.

rows.name: Paper strip creatures (3D zoo)
steps: Make 3D creatures using paper strips and forms by folding, curling and stacking.
Join parts using tabs, slots and bridges.
Show the finished work to a partner and say what was made.
rows.materials: Not listed in the document (paper strips, card)

levels.0: Creature lies flat on the table, or its parts fall apart when lifted.
levels.1: Creature stands up after the educator holds a tab or slot while the child fixes it.
levels.2: Creature stands on its own, built with folded, curled and stacked paper joined by tabs and slots.
levels.3: Paper strip creatures 3D: the child builds a second creature for a new job, such as a bridge, and explains how the pieces hold.

rows.name: Pinch pot or story plate in clay or dough
steps: Make a pinch pot or story plate by pinching, rolling, pressing or coiling clay or dough.
If festive, make an eco-friendly diya, animal or character.
Show the finished work to a partner and say what was made.

levels.0: Clay piece crumbles or has no clear shape, and no pinch, roll or coil mark is made.
levels.1: Pot shape appears after the educator shows the pinch, and coils are added with help.
levels.2: Pot or plate holds its shape and shows pinched walls and a rolled or coiled edge.
levels.3: Models a new shape such as a diya and tells which clay technique made each part.

rows.name: Portfolio building
steps: Organise works into folders.
Choose 3 pieces you are most proud of.
Fill in mini reflection sheets (Why did I choose this? What I learned?).

levels.0: Folder holds loose, unsorted work, and fewer than three pieces are picked.
levels.1: Three pieces are picked but need the educator to help put them in order in the folder.
levels.2: Folder holds three chosen pieces in order, each with a filled reflection sheet naming what was learned.
levels.3: Gives reasons for choosing the pieces and moves one to a different order to show growth.

rows.name: The Broken Robot Artist: make the robot draw a square
steps: The educator stands at the whiteboard as a drawing robot with a marker and asks the class to make the robot draw a perfect square; a child calls out the first instruction.
A vague instruction such as 'Draw a line' makes the robot draw a messy squiggle; children try again and say how far and which direction.
An instruction with no stop, such as 'Draw a straight line across', makes the robot run off the board; children give exact numbers, for example 'to the right for 30 centimetres and then stop'.
The instruction 'Turn!' makes the robot spin all the way round; children say the exact turn needed, a 90-degree turn, and the class agrees that computers cannot guess.

levels.0: Calls out 'draw a line' or 'turn' with no distance, direction or angle, so the robot-educator draws a squiggle.
levels.1: Adds a distance or a turn only after the educator prompts 'how far?' or 'which way?', and forgets where to stop.
levels.2: Instruction names a direction, an exact distance and a stop, such as 'right 30 centimetres then stop', and the robot draws it correctly.
levels.3: Corrects a classmate's vague command aloud and explains why the robot needs a 90-degree turn instead of just 'turn'.

rows.name: ScratchJr Grid Navigators: move the frog to the fly
steps: Tech Log set up: sketch a 4x4 square grid, colour 3 random squares blue for water tiles, and draw a small frog at the bottom left and a fly at the top right.
Tap the Grid Icon at the top of the ScratchJr screen; the numbers on the grid match the numbers typed into the motion blocks.
Select an animal sprite and program it to move from its starting position to the target item without touching the marked water tiles.
Count the grid squares: if the frog needs to move 6 squares, change the number in the block from 1 to 6, and put the number in one block instead of snapping a long train of Move Right 1 blocks.
rows.materials: Tech Log notebook, ScratchJr with its grid icon, animal sprite

levels.0: Snaps a long train of Move Right 1 blocks and the frog still ends up on a blue water tile.
levels.1: Reaches the fly only after the educator points to the grid numbers and reminds the child to count squares.
levels.2: Frog reaches the fly avoiding every water tile, with one block set to the counted number of squares.
levels.3: Explains to a partner why one Move 3 block does the work of three Move 1 blocks and finds a second route.

rows.name: Island Grid Navigator worksheet: pick the bug-free algorithm
steps: Look at the grid map: Monkey must reach the Banana and cannot walk onto the dark grey mud tiles.
Read the three algorithm options (Option A, B and C), each a list of Move steps.

levels.1: Circles the safe option only after tracing each route and being reminded which tiles are mud.
levels.2: Circled option takes Monkey to the banana avoiding mud, with the route traced on the grid.
levels.3: Writes a different bug-free move list for the same map and says why the other options hit mud.

rows.name: Human Keyboard game
steps: Explain that a clap or stomp is an input, and what the room does back is an output.
When the educator claps once (input), the room shouts 'Beep!' (output).
When the educator stomps a foot (input), the room jumps up (output).
Let children take turns giving the input, then ask the class to name the input and the output each time.

levels.0: In the game, the room responds to the wrong signal or cannot say which action was the signal and which the response.
levels.1: Pointing to the clap or stomp with the educator's help, signal and response are named for one round.
levels.2: Both rounds are described with a clear signal as input and a response as output, such as stomp then jump.
levels.3: Invents a new input and output pair for the game and links it to a device shown in a picture.

rows.name: ScratchJr: Start on Tap trigger
steps: Hand out tablets with ScratchJr open and talk about real-world inputs such as touching a screen.
In the tech log, children identify real-world inputs and draw a tablet screen being tapped by a finger.
Children build a program with the Start on Tap trigger block, coding a sprite to stay still until tapped, then spin or grow.
Children tap their sprite for a partner and name the input and the output.

levels.0: Sprite moves at once or not at all when tapped, and the tablet drawing shows no finger input or screen output.
levels.1: Shown the trigger block by a partner, the sprite starts on tap but the tap is not named as input.

rows.name: Paper flipbook animation
steps: Prepare a simple 3-page paper flipbook of a stick figure waving its arm.

Children say what changed from page to page, and try the flipbook themselves.

levels.0: Describes the flipbook as one picture or says nothing changes between pages, with no mention of frames.
levels.1: Flipping slowly alongside the educator, one change between two pages, such as arm position, is named.

Children program a sequence that keeps changing the costume so it looks like flying or hopping across the backdrop, then show a partner.

levels.1: Partner help adding costumes lets the sprite swap between two poses once without repeating.
levels.2: Sprite's costume frames change in sequence as it travels across the backdrop, so it looks like flying or hopping.
levels.3: Adds a start event such as a tap and adjusts frame timing, explaining which blocks give a smoother hop.

Children trace the line that connects different animal costume frames in logical order.
Partners compare traced lines and explain why they put the frames in that order.

levels.0: Traced line joins frames in a jumbled order, skips frames, or stops after one picture.
levels.1: Given the first frame by the educator, the line joins two or three frames in order before going wrong.
levels.2: The traced line joins all costume frames in the order that makes the animal appear to move.
levels.3: Explains why frames must run in that order and rearranges a mixed set of new frames correctly.

rows.name: Loops: five jumping jacks

levels.1: Counting lines aloud with the educator, the Repeat 5 version is picked as shorter but no reason is given.
levels.2: Compares the five-line list with Repeat 5 and says the repeat uses fewer lines for the same five jumping jacks.
levels.3: Rewrites a different repeated action, such as clapping seven times, using Repeat and says how many lines it saves.

Play the project to show a working loop to your partner.

levels.1: Places a repeat block but the count or the enclosed blocks need the educator's help to match the original.
levels.2: Script uses a repeat block with fewer blocks than before and the sprite gives the same movement.
levels.3: Counts blocks before and after the change and explains in own words how many blocks the loop saved.

rows.name: Count the steps in a Repeat 3 loop
steps: Write 'Repeat 3: Move 2 steps' on the board and have a child act it out.
Hand out the worksheet and ask children to count the total steps a character moves if it runs Move 2 steps inside a Repeat 3 loop.
Children show their working, by drawing the hops or writing the sum.
Partners compare totals and explain how they counted.

levels.0: Answer given is 2 or 3, showing only one number from the loop was used.
levels.1: Seeing three hops drawn on a line by the educator, steps are counted one by one to reach the total.
levels.2: Total of 6 steps is found for Repeat 3 with Move 2, shown by repeated addition or multiplication.
levels.3: Works out the total for a new Repeat count or step size and writes the matching shorter program.

rows.name: Debug a maze script step by step
steps: Draw a maze with dead ends on the board, with a long messy script beside it containing two errors.
Children test the path step by step with a finger, following the script line by line.
Stop where the code loses track, and children suggest what each error is and how to fix it.
As a class, rewrite the script with fewer blocks that still reach the exit.

levels.0: Finger path does not follow the script line by line, so the two errors stay unfound.
levels.1: Stopping at each line with the educator, one error is spotted but the other stays in the rewrite.
levels.2: Both errors are found by tracing and the script is rewritten with fewer blocks that still reach the maze exit.
levels.3: Explains where the messy script wasted steps and writes a shorter, correct script for a new maze.

Children step through the script to find the missing trigger block and rebuild the connection, then show a partner it now works.

Partners compare circles and explain how they knew that join was broken.

levels.1: Tracing the first joins with the educator, the broken connector is circled in the shortest series only.
levels.2: Circle lands exactly on the broken puzzle connector in each series of ScratchJr blocks.
levels.3: Says what would happen when the script runs with the break, and draws the repaired join.

rows.name: Subtraction Bowling
steps: Set up pins that each have a number on them.
Roll a ball and add up the numbers on the pins knocked down.
Subtract that total from a target number.
Write the subtraction and check it with addition.
rows.materials: Place value charts, dice, pins with numbers

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan

levels.3: Checks a subtraction by adding back and explains why the check proves the answer.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!9. Calculating: Addition and Subtraction of 3/4 Digit Numbers – Period 2; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Dice Roll Word Problems
steps: Roll dice to make two numbers.
Write a short word problem using the two numbers.
Swap problems with a partner.
Solve the partner's problem with a number sentence.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan
source.cell: 9. Calculating: Addition and Subtraction of 3/4 Digit Numbers – Period 3

levels.0: Writes a story with two numbers but no question, so the partner cannot tell what to find.
levels.1: Solves a swapped problem only when the educator picks out the key number words with them.
levels.2: Writes a word problem from the dice numbers and solves a partner's with a number sentence.
levels.3: Writes a problem for a different operation and shows two ways to solve it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!9. Calculating: Addition and Subtraction of 3/4 Digit Numbers – Period 3; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Array Building with cubes
steps: Pick a multiplication fact, such as 3 × 4.
Build it as rows of cubes.
Count the cubes in all.
Draw the array on squared paper.
rows.materials: Counters, cubes, multiplication charts, squared paper

levels.3: Builds two different arrays for 12 and explains how both show the same total.

rows.name: Sharing Game with bowls
steps: Count out candies (or counters) in a pile.
Share them out one at a time into bowls until none are left.
Count how many are in each bowl.
Tell whether each bowl has the same amount.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan

levels.0: Puts more candies in one bowl and says every bowl is the same.
levels.1: Shares equally only with the educator saying 'one for you, one for you' for each bowl.
levels.2: Shares the candies equally into bowls and says how many are in each.
levels.3: Shares an odd number between bowls, finds a remainder and explains what it means.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!10. Multiplication and Division; Times Table 1–10 – Period 2; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Times Table Hopscotch
steps: Chalk a hopscotch grid outdoors with the numbers of a times table.
Hop on each square and say the fact aloud.
Count on in the table as you hop to the end.
Swap turns with a partner who checks your answers.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan
source.cell: 10. Multiplication and Division; Times Table 1–10 – Period 3

levels.2: Says each fact of the 2, 5 or 10 table aloud without counting as they hop.
levels.3: Hops and says a table the partner chooses, including 3s and 4s, without pausing.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!10. Multiplication and Division; Times Table 1–10 – Period 3; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Angle Hunt
steps: Make a right-angle checker from the corner of a paper.
Go around the room finding corners that match.
Write down or draw each right angle you find.
Share your best three with the group.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan

levels.0: Points to a sloped roof corner as a right angle and does not test it with the paper corner.
levels.1: Tests corners with the paper only when the educator names which objects to try.
levels.2: Finds and names several right angles in the room by checking with a paper corner.
levels.3: Finds angles that are not right angles and tells whether each is smaller or larger than the paper corner.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!11. Geometry: Angles and Turns, Circles – Period 1; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Turn Game with toy cars
steps: Place a toy car on a path.
The educator calls a quarter turn, half turn or full turn.
Turn the car through the turn called.
Take turns calling turns for a partner.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan
source.cell: 11. Geometry: Angles and Turns, Circles – Period 2

levels.0: Turns the car a full circle when a quarter turn is called.
levels.1: Makes quarter and half turns only when the educator shows a model turn first.
levels.2: Turns the car through a quarter, half or full turn as called.
levels.3: Calls turns for a partner and says what direction the car faces afterwards.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!11. Geometry: Angles and Turns, Circles – Period 2; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Pour and Measure
steps: Choose containers of different sizes.
Fill one with water and pour it into a measuring jug.
Read the level on the jug in ml or L.
Compare the capacity of two containers.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan

levels.0: Reads the water level at the top of the jug instead of at the surface of the water.
levels.1: Reads the jug scale only when the educator points to the line and says the unit.
levels.2: Pours water into a measuring jug and reads the capacity in ml or L correctly.
levels.3: Predicts which of two containers holds more, pours to check, and explains the result.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!12. Measures: Mass, Capacity, Temperature – Period 2; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Pattern Necklaces
steps: Choose coloured beads for a pattern, such as red, blue, red, blue.
Thread the beads in a repeating pattern.
Say the pattern aloud.
Show the pattern to a partner and name what repeats.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan

levels.0: Threads beads where the colours do not repeat in the same order and does not notice.
levels.1: Continues a bead pattern only when the first two repeats are already threaded for them.
levels.2: Threads a repeating bead pattern and names the part that repeats.
levels.3: Threads a pattern of three kinds, such as ABC or AAB, and explains how to predict the next bead.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!13. Pattern and Probability – Period 1; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Probability Sorting
steps: Take a set of event cards.
Place each under certain, likely, unlikely or impossible.
Compare your choices with a partner.
Give one new event for each group.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan

levels.0: Puts 'the sun will rise tomorrow' under impossible and does not move it after discussion.
levels.1: Places only 'certain' and 'impossible' cards; likely and unlikely cards need the educator's help.
levels.2: Sorts event cards into certain, likely, unlikely and impossible correctly.
levels.3: Makes up new events for each group and says why each belongs where it is placed.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!13. Pattern and Probability – Period 3; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Mirror Art
steps: Draw half of a picture on one side of a fold line.
Place a mirror on the line to see the whole picture.
Draw the other half to match.
Check your drawing with the mirror.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan

levels.0: Draws the second half facing the same way as the first, so the two halves do not match in the mirror.
levels.1: Completes the other half only with the educator marking dots on the grid for each point.
levels.2: Completes the missing half of a picture so it matches in a mirror.
levels.3: Draws a new picture with its own line of symmetry and proves it with a mirror.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!14. Symmetry, Position, and Movement – Period 1; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Treasure Hunt with map directions
steps: Hide an object and draw a simple map of its place.
Write directions such as forward, left and right on the map.
A partner follows the directions to find the object.
Fix any direction that sent your partner the wrong way.

source.tab: Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan

levels.0: Writes 'left' where the partner needed to go right, so the partner ends far from the hidden object.
levels.1: Gives directions only for the first few steps and needs the educator to supply the rest.
levels.2: Writes directions on a map that lead a partner to the hidden object.
levels.3: Gives directions with distances and fixes a mistake after watching the partner follow them.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 Cambridge Primary Mathematics: Project-Based and Concrete Learning Plan!14. Symmetry, Position, and Movement – Period 3; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Timeline of our school day
steps: Choose five events from the school day, such as arrival, assembly and lunch.
Draw each event on a card.
Stick the cards in time order along a paper timeline.
Tell a partner what happened first, next and last.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Sticks the lunch card before assembly and does not change it when the partner reads the timeline.
levels.1: Places cards in sequence only when the educator names the first and last events for them.
levels.2: Sticks five event cards in the correct order along a timeline.
levels.3: Adds events from another day, such as a school trip, and explains why each belongs before or after.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 1–2: Introduction to History; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Visit to a local historical site
steps: Visit a local historical site with the class.
Look at it closely and take notes or draw what you see.
Write or tell the name of the site.
Share one thing you saw with the group.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Gives a name that belongs to a different place when asked what the site was called.
levels.1: Names the site only when the educator says the first sound or shows its picture.
levels.2: Names the local site visited and tells one thing about it in own words.
levels.3: Compares the site with another landmark in the city and explains why people visit both.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 3–4: Our Local History; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Scrapbook of local festivals
steps: Choose a local festival.
Draw or stick a picture of how it is celebrated.
Write its name and one line about it beside the picture.
Add the page to a class scrapbook.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Writes a festival name beside a picture of a different festival and leaves it unchanged.
levels.1: Fills a page only when the educator gives the festival name and the picture to stick.
levels.2: Makes a scrapbook page with a picture, the festival's name and one line about it.
levels.3: Adds a page comparing two festivals and explains one way they are alike and one way they differ.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 3–4: Our Local History; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Community elders storytelling
steps: Invite a community elder to the class to tell a story from the past.
Listen quietly and note one thing you heard.
Ask the elder one question.
Tell a partner the part you liked best.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Talks about a different story when asked what the elder said and cannot repeat any part.
levels.1: Repeats part of the story only after the educator reminds them of the characters.
levels.2: Tells what they think of the elder's story and gives one detail they heard.
levels.3: Compares the elder's story with another story and explains how life then differs from now.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 3–4: Our Local History; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Model of an ancient dwelling
steps: Decide which ancient dwelling to build, such as an Indus Valley house.
Build the model with clay, cardboard or blocks.
Label the parts of the house.
Show the model to the group and say how it kept people safe.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Builds a house with no door or roof and does not notice when asked how people would go in.
levels.1: Assembles the walls only when a picture is shown beside them and names the parts when asked.
levels.2: Builds a model dwelling with labelled parts and names it correctly.
levels.3: Constructs a second model for a different place and explains how each house suited its land.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 5–6: Early Civilizations; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Map ancient trade routes
steps: Suggested: Look at a simple map of the region.
Suggested: Mark the places where goods were made.
Draw lines between the places to show where traders carried goods.
Suggested: Tell a partner what was traded on one route.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Route lines join places at random and no goods are named for any route.
levels.1: Draws a route only when the educator names the two places to join, and names no goods.
levels.2: Draws a route between two marked places and names the goods carried along it.
levels.3: Plans a route for new goods, names what is carried and says why traders chose that way.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 5–6: Early Civilizations; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Role-play events from leaders' lives
steps: Choose a leader from the class list, such as Mahatma Gandhi or Rani Lakshmibai.
Listen to a short story of one event from the leader's life.
Act out the event in a small group.
Say what the leader did and why it mattered.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Acts the event without naming the leader and cannot say what the leader did.
levels.1: Joins the role-play only when the educator tells them their lines and actions.
levels.2: Acts out an event and says one value the leader showed.
levels.3: Describes a value from the role-play and explains how it could be used in the school today.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 7–8: Famous Leaders; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Posters of leaders' achievements
steps: Choose a leader to show.
Draw the leader and write their name.
Write or draw two achievements.
Display your poster and tell the class about one achievement.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Draws a leader's picture with a wrong name beside it and does not correct it.
levels.1: Fills in the poster only with the educator pointing to the facts on a fact card.
levels.2: Makes a poster with the leader's name, a picture and two achievements.
levels.3: Explains what value links two leaders' achievements and shows it on a joint poster.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 7–8: Famous Leaders; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Cultural dress-up day
steps: Choose a region of India to show.
Wear or hold something from that region's dress.
Say the region's name and one thing about its dress.
Look at three classmates' regions and ask a question.
rows.materials: Dress items from home or school

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Names the region wrongly and cannot say one thing about its dress when asked.
levels.1: Names the region only after looking at a map the educator holds.
levels.2: Shows regional dress and says the region's name and one thing about it.
levels.3: Compares dress from two regions and explains one reason why they differ.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 9–10: Cultural Diversity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Festival calendar
steps: Make a 12-month calendar page.
Mark the month of each major festival.
Draw a small picture for each.
Show your calendar and tell one festival's month.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Marks Diwali in a month where it does not fall and keeps it after the calendar is checked.
levels.1: Marks festivals only with the educator saying the month and pointing to the box.
levels.2: Marks festivals in the correct months with a picture for each.
levels.3: Plans a class celebration on a chosen date and counts the weeks to it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 11–12: Festivals and Celebrations; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Transport timeline
steps: Look at cards of transport: bullock cart, bicycle, train, aeroplane.
Put the cards in the order they came into use.
Stick them on a timeline.
Tell a partner how one change helped people.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Puts the aeroplane before the bullock cart and leaves the order after the partner questions it.
levels.1: Orders two or three cards after the educator tells them the first and last ones.
levels.2: Sticks transport cards in the correct time order along a timeline.
levels.3: Places a new mode of transport on the timeline and explains how it changed daily life.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 13–14: Transportation Through Time; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Old and new communication devices
steps: Look at pictures of old and new devices, such as a letter, a telephone and a mobile phone.
Sort them into old and new.
Match each to the job it does.
Tell a partner one way the new device is different.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Puts the mobile phone in the old group and does not move it after the partner points to the date.
levels.1: Names the devices only when the educator says the first sound or shows what it does.
levels.2: Sorts devices into old and new and names what each one does.
levels.3: Traces how a device changed over time and what people did before it was invented.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 15–16: Communication Evolution; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Write a letter the traditional way
steps: Take paper and a pen.
Write a short letter to a classmate with a greeting and a sign-off.
Fold and place the letter in a class post box.
Read the letter you receive.

source.tab: Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Writes a letter with no greeting or sign-off and does not add them when the model is shown.
levels.1: Writes the greeting and sign-off only by copying from a model letter on the board.
levels.2: Writes a short letter with a greeting, a message and a sign-off.
levels.3: Writes a reply to a received letter that answers the sender's question.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Fortnight 15–16: Communication Evolution; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Traditional games: lagori and spinning top
steps: Learn the rules of a traditional game such as lagori or spinning top.
Play in small groups.
Say how it differs from a toy you know today.
Take turns teaching a friend one rule.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Plays the game without the stated rule and does not stop when the partner reminds them.
levels.1: Plays only with the educator calling each step and tells no difference from a toy of today.
levels.2: Plays a traditional game and says one difference from a toy today.
levels.3: Explains why children played this game long ago and compares its materials with a modern toy.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Toys from the Past; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Make a simple toy: paper doll or top
steps: Choose to make a paper doll or a top.
Cut and fold paper or card.
Decorate it.
Try it out and show it to a friend.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Folds the paper so the toy does not stand or spin and tries it again without changing the fold.
levels.1: Makes the toy only when the educator folds the first step for them.
levels.2: Makes a paper doll or top that stands or spins.
levels.3: Makes a second toy of their own design and explains how it is like a toy of the past.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Toys from the Past; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Toy museum corner
steps: Bring in an old toy or look at the educator's collection.
Place each toy in the museum corner with a name card.
Walk around and look at the toys.
Tell a partner how one old toy differs from a toy today.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Says an old wooden top is the same as a new toy and gives no difference.
levels.1: Names one difference only after the educator points to the materials of both toys.
levels.2: Compares a toy from the past with one today and tells one difference.
levels.3: Tells how a toy changed over time and why, with two differences from their own observation.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Toys from the Past; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Early human cave painting

Draw an animal or hunting scene in earth colours on brown paper.
Show your picture and say what it tells.
Pin the pictures up as a cave wall.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.1: Draws an animal only by tracing and says what early humans did only after prompting.
levels.2: Draws a cave painting and tells one way early humans met their needs from it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Early Humans; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Role play: hunter and gatherer
steps: Split into two groups, hunters and gatherers.
Act out finding food, one group with spears and the other with baskets.
Return to the cave and share the food.
Say which job you did and why it mattered.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Acts as a hunter picking fruit and does not change when the educator names the job again.
levels.1: Joins the role play only when told what to do next and names one job after prompting.
levels.2: Acts a hunter or a gatherer and says what the job gave to the group.
levels.3: Says how the two groups depended on each other and what would happen without one.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Early Humans; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Survival sorting game

Say why you placed two cards.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

rows.name: Make clay tools

Shape clay into one of the tools.
Say what job the tool does.
Show it to the group.

levels.2: Shapes a clay tool and says in a sentence why early humans needed tools.
levels.3: Shows how a tool helped early humans with food and safety, giving two examples.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Discovery of Fire & Tools; some steps were added by the worker

steps: Look at picture cards showing tasks, such as cutting and hunting.

Check each other's piles.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.3: Tells why a tool made a job easier and picks a card to prove it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Discovery of Fire & Tools; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Build huts with sticks and leaves
steps: Gather sticks and leaves.

Check that it has a roof and a door.
Tell the group how the hut keeps you safe.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.1: Builds the walls only when the educator holds the sticks and says where to put the roof.
levels.2: Builds a small hut and says how it keeps people safe and dry.
levels.3: Compares their hut with a cave and explains one good thing about each as shelter.

rows.name: Compare a cave and a modern house
steps: Look at a picture of a cave and a picture of a house.
List two things the same and two different.
Share your list with a partner.
Say which one you would choose and why.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Says a cave has a television and does not change it when the picture is looked at again.
levels.1: Lists a difference only after the educator asks about doors, roof or light.
levels.2: Compares a cave and a house with two likenesses and two differences.
levels.3: Gives reasons why people moved from caves to houses using shelter and safety.

rows.name: City model with blocks

Lay out roads with blocks in straight lines.
Add blocks as houses along the roads.
Say how the plan helped people.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.2: Builds a city model with straight roads and houses and names them.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Indus Valley Civilization; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Barter game
steps: Each child gets an item to trade.
Walk around and exchange your item for one you want, without using money.
Say what you gave and what you got.
Talk about whether the swap was fair.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Says money was used in the barter and does not notice that nothing was bought.
levels.1: Swaps an item only when the educator pairs them with a partner and says the rule.
levels.2: Exchanges one item for another and says what they gave and got.
levels.3: Explains why barter can be hard when each person wants a different thing.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Trade & Agriculture; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Seed planting
steps: Fill a small pot with soil.
Plant a seed and water it.
Place the pot in a sunny spot.
Look after it for a week and draw how it grows.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Plants a seed on top of dry soil and does not water it after being asked about it.
levels.1: Plants the seed only when the educator says each step in order.
levels.2: Plants a seed and draws how it grows in pictures in order.
levels.3: Explains how early people used seeds to grow food and why that made them stay in one place.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Trade & Agriculture; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Role play: farmer and trader
steps: Choose to be a farmer or a trader.
The farmer grows a crop (picture) and the trader brings goods.
Exchange the crop for goods.
Say what each of you needed.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Plays the trader but gives goods away without asking for a crop and does not notice.
levels.1: Joins the exchange only when the educator tells them what to say.
levels.2: Acts a farmer or a trader and explains what was exchanged.
levels.3: Explains why farmers and traders needed each other and what could go wrong.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Trade & Agriculture; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Occupation charades
steps: Take an occupation card, such as potter or farmer.
Act the job without speaking.
The class guesses the job.
Say if the job is old or still done today.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Acts a potter as a farmer and does not change after the class guesses wrongly.
levels.1: Acts a job only after the educator whispers the first action.
levels.2: Acts a job and says whether it was done long ago or is still done.
levels.3: Compares an old job with a similar job today and explains one change.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Occupations Then and Now; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Paper weaving
steps: Cut slits in a sheet of paper.
Weave a paper strip over and under.
Add more strips in an over-under pattern.
Show your woven mat and say who weaves for work.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Weaves two strips over the same way and does not see the pattern break.
levels.1: Weaves the first two strips only when the educator shows the pattern.
levels.2: Weaves strips in an over-under pattern into a paper mat.
levels.3: Weaves a different pattern and explains how weavers made cloth long ago.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Occupations Then and Now; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Landmark study
steps: Look at pictures of a Pune landmark.
Draw the landmark.
Write its name under your drawing.
Tell the group what the place is for.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Draws a landmark but names a different one beside it.
levels.1: Names a Pune landmark only after seeing its picture beside a name card.
levels.2: Draws a Pune landmark and writes its name.
levels.3: Explains why the landmark matters to the people of Pune in a sentence of their own.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Local History (Pune Focus); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Map marking of local places
steps: Look at a simple map of Pune.
Mark the school.
Mark a landmark with a sticker.
Tell a partner how to go from the school to it.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Places the landmark sticker in the sea on the map and does not move it.
levels.1: Places stickers only with the educator pointing to the right square.
levels.2: Marks the school and a landmark on a map correctly.
levels.3: Gives directions between two marked places using left, right and straight.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Local History (Pune Focus); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Story enactment: Akbar and Birbal or Tenali Raman
steps: Listen to a story of Akbar and Birbal or Tenali Raman.
Choose a part and practise with a group.
Act out the story with puppets or drama.
Say what the story teaches.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Acts a character but changes the story's ending and does not notice when asked.
levels.1: Acts a part only with the educator giving each line and cue.
levels.2: Acts the story and says what they think about it.
levels.3: Explains the lesson and tells how another story could teach it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Historical Stories & Legends; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Picture sequencing of a story
steps: Look at picture cards from a story.
Put them in the right order.
Retell the story using the pictures.
Check the order with a partner.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Puts the last picture first and retells a story that does not match their order.
levels.1: Orders the first two pictures and needs the educator to help with the rest.
levels.2: Puts the story pictures in order and tells what happens.
levels.3: Retells the story from a mixed set and adds what they think of it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Historical Stories & Legends; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Timeline cards: wheel to phone
steps: Take cards: wheel, fire, bulb, phone.
Put them in order.
Stick them on a timeline.
Say how one invention changed life.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Sticks the phone card before the wheel and does not change it when the order is read aloud.
levels.1: Orders two cards and needs the educator to place the rest.
levels.2: Puts invention cards in order and names each invention.
levels.3: Explains how one invention changed life and what people did before it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Inventions That Changed Life; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Hero badge making
steps: Choose a hero or role model from a story.
Draw a badge for them.
Write one good value on the badge, such as courage.
Share your badge with a partner.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)
source.cell: Inventions That Changed Life (World Heroes & Role Models)

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Inventions That Changed Life (World Heroes & Role Models); some steps were added by the worker
look_fors: Names a value, such as courage, that a hero showed in the story.
Draws a badge that matches the value they named.
Tells a partner one action of the hero that showed that value.

rows.name: Kindness collage
steps: Cut pictures of kind actions from old magazines.
Stick them on a class collage.
Add a word for each action.
Say one kind action you can do in class.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!World Heroes & Role Models; some steps were added by the worker
look_fors: Points to a kind action in a picture and names it.
Shares glue or scissors without being asked.
Says one kind action to do in class and does it later.

rows.name: Mini museum
steps: Choose something learned this year to show.
Make a model, drawing or object for the mini museum.
Write a label for it.
Visit other displays and tell one thing you learned.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Brings a display with no label and cannot say what it shows when asked.
levels.1: Prepares a display only with the educator helping with the label.
levels.2: Makes a museum item with a label and says what it shows.
levels.3: Explains their item to a visitor and answers one question about it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Project & Celebration; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: History booklet
steps: Fold paper into a small booklet.
Draw a picture from each topic learned this year.
Write one sentence under each picture.
Show your booklet to a partner.

source.tab: Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)

levels.0: Draws pictures with sentences that do not match the pictures and leaves them.
levels.1: Writes sentences under pictures only by copying words from the board.
levels.2: Makes a booklet with pictures and a sentence for each topic.
levels.3: Explains how two topics are linked and adds a page to show it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 History Curriculum (Cambridge Primary – Indian Context)!Project & Celebration; doc names the activity only, steps were added

rows.name: No Technology Challenge
steps: Look at pictures of a mobile, pizza, house and fire.
Think what would happen if these all disappeared today.
Share how you would stay alive with a partner.

source.cell: Session 1 (45 Minutes) – Who Were the Early Humans?

levels.0: Names a phone as the way early humans kept warm and does not change it after discussion.
levels.1: Suggests a way to survive only after the educator reads out food, shelter and safety.
levels.2: Describes one way to find food or shelter without technology.
levels.3: Compares life without technology with life of early humans and explains one challenge.

rows.note: named in Histor Grade 2-4 (History plan 2026)!Session 1 (45 Minutes) – Who Were the Early Humans?; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Survival Stations
steps: Station 1 Food Sorting: sort pictures into edible and not edible.
Station 2 Build a Cave: use blocks or paper.
Station 3 Stone Tool Detective: match each tool to its purpose (hunting, cutting, digging).
Station 4 Animal Danger: sort animal cards into friendly and dangerous.
rows.materials: Pictures of caves, stone tools, animal cards, blocks or paper

source.cell: Session 1 (45 Minutes) – Who Were the Early Humans?

levels.0: Puts a poisonous plant under edible at the food station and keeps it there.
levels.1: Completes one station only when the educator names the cards and says where each goes.
levels.2: Completes the stations and says one way early humans found food or shelter.
levels.3: Explains how three stations showed that early humans needed food, shelter and safety.

rows.note: Document gives four stations as steps; materials as listed.

rows.name: Become Archaeologists
steps: Find artefact pictures (stone tools, animal cards, paper bones) buried in the sand tray.
Dig and identify each artefact.
Say what each tells about early humans.
rows.materials: Sand tray, stone tool pictures, animal cards, paper bones

source.cell: Session 2 (45 Minutes) – How Early Humans Changed the World

levels.0: Calls a paper bone a plant and does not link it to food when asked.
levels.1: Names an artefact only after the educator shows a matching card.
levels.2: Identifies the artefacts and says what one tells about early humans.
levels.3: Explains what the group of finds says about how the people lived.

rows.note: named in Histor Grade 2-4 (History plan 2026)!Session 2 (45 Minutes) – How Early Humans Changed the World; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Cave Art Gallery
steps: Take brown chart paper.
Draw hunting scenes, animals, handprints or a campfire.
Use only brown, black, red and yellow.
Display the pictures as a gallery and explain one.
rows.materials: Brown chart paper, brown, black, red and yellow colours

source.cell: Session 2 (45 Minutes) – How Early Humans Changed the World

levels.0: Picture shows no hunting, animal, handprint or fire scene, and nothing is said about early life
levels.1: Draws one cave-style figure and names what early humans did only after the educator's question
levels.2: Cave picture shows a hunting, animal or campfire scene and the child says how it helped early humans get food, warmth or safety
levels.3: Compares the cave scene with how needs are met today and explains why early humans painted on walls

rows.note: named in Histor Grade 2-4 (History plan 2026)!Session 2 (45 Minutes) – How Early Humans Changed the World; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Timeline Race
steps: Take the cards: Stone Tools, Fire, Cave Paintings, Farming.
Arrange them in the order they were discovered.
Race another group to finish and check the order.

source.cell: Session 2 (45 Minutes) – How Early Humans Changed the World

levels.0: Puts Farming first and does not change it when the other group reads their order.
levels.1: Arranges the cards only after the educator names the first and last discovery.
levels.2: Arranges the cards in the order they were discovered.
levels.3: Explains why fire came before farming and how each discovery helped the next.

rows.note: named in Histor Grade 2-4 (History plan 2026)!Session 2 (45 Minutes) – How Early Humans Changed the World; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Can You Survive? inquiry project
steps: Each group gets a place: forest, desert, snow or grassland.
Plan shelter, food, clothing and safety for that place.
Present your survival plan to the class.

levels.0: Plan names one need such as food and leaves out shelter and clothing.
levels.1: Plans shelter or food only after the educator suggests the other needs.
levels.2: Chart shows shelter, food and clothing planned for the given place.
levels.3: Chart explains how the place changed each choice and compares it with another group's plan.

rows.note: Document gives the project; all steps are the document's own.

rows.name: Globe spinning: find India
steps: Spin the globe gently.
Stop it with a finger.
Say if you found India.
Take turns until each child finds India.

source.cell: Fortnight 1–2: India on the Globe and States of India (Intro)

levels.0: Points to Africa and says it is India and does not change after seeing the flag.
levels.1: Finds India only when the educator names the country next to it.
levels.2: Finds and points to India on the globe.
levels.3: Finds India and names two countries that touch it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 - Geography Curriculum!Fortnight 1–2: India on the Globe and States of India (Intro); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: India puzzle and colour your state
steps: Put together a puzzle of India's states.
Find your own state.
Colour it.
Tell a partner its name.

source.cell: Fortnight 1–2: India on the Globe and States of India (Intro)

levels.0: Colours a different state from their own and does not correct it when shown the name.
levels.1: Finds their state only when the educator points to its label.
levels.2: Names their own state and colours it on a map of India.
levels.3: Names a neighbouring state and says where it lies compared with their own.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 - Geography Curriculum!Fortnight 1–2: India on the Globe and States of India (Intro); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: State symbols collage
steps: Look at pictures of state symbols.
Cut out the symbols.
Stick them on a collage with the state name.
Share one symbol.

source.cell: Fortnight 1–2: India on the Globe and States of India (Intro)

levels.0: Sticks symbols of another state beside their own and does not move them.
levels.1: Sticks symbols only when the educator hands them the right ones.
levels.2: Makes a collage naming their state with its symbols.
levels.3: Names a symbol of another state and tells which state it belongs to.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 - Geography Curriculum!Fortnight 1–2: India on the Globe and States of India (Intro); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Globe: land versus water
steps: Look at the globe.
Touch the land with one finger and water with another.
Name three continents.
Name the oceans you can find.

levels.0: Points to the ocean and calls it land and does not change it after touching the globe.
levels.1: Shows land and water only when the educator says each one.
levels.2: Points to land and water and names several continents or oceans.
levels.3: Names all five oceans and the continents beside each.

rows.name: Colour continents and paint oceans
steps: Take an outline world map.
Colour each continent a different colour.
Paint the oceans blue.
Say the names of the continents.

levels.0: Paints a continent blue and does not see the mistake after looking at the globe.
levels.1: Colours continents only when the educator names each one.
levels.2: Colours the continents and paints the oceans blue on the map.
levels.3: Names the oceans on their map and the continents beside them.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 - Geography Curriculum!Fortnight 3–4: Continents & Oceans; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Circle Asia, stick India
steps: Circle Asia on a world map.
Place a sticker on India.
Say 'India is in Asia'.
Compare the size of Asia with other continents by looking.

levels.0: Circles Africa and says it is Asia and keeps it after looking again.
levels.1: Circles Asia only after the educator names the shape.
levels.2: Circles Asia and places the sticker on India.
levels.3: Explains where India lies in Asia and names one other Asian country.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 - Geography Curriculum!Fortnight 5-6: Continent Asia & India’s Place; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Landform picture card sort
steps: Look at the physical map's colours: green, brown, yellow.
Take picture cards of mountains, plains, deserts and plateaus.
Sort them into four groups.
Match each landform to a real image.

levels.0: Puts a mountain card under desert and does not move it after matching to the map.
levels.1: Sorts only mountains and plains and needs the educator for the others.
levels.2: Sorts landform cards into mountain, plain, desert and plateau using the map key.
levels.3: Describes each landform as high, flat or dry and gives an example in India.

rows.name: Clay modelling of landforms
steps: Take clay.
Shape a mountain and a plain.
Label each with a card.
Show your model to a partner.

levels.0: Shapes both landforms flat and cannot tell which is the mountain.
levels.1: Shapes a mountain only by copying a model and labels after help.
levels.2: Shapes landforms from clay and labels each.
levels.3: Adds a plateau and explains how it differs from a mountain.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 - Geography Curriculum!Fortnight 7-8: Physical Features of India; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: River versus sea picture sorting
steps: Look at pictures of rivers and seas.
Sort them into two groups.
Trace a river on a simple map with your finger.
Tell one difference.

source.cell: Fortnight 9-10: Water Bodies – Rivers and Seas

levels.0: Sorts a river with the seas and does not move it after the partner shows the picture.
levels.1: Groups only the clearest pictures and needs the educator to help with the rest.
levels.2: Sorts rivers and seas correctly and tells one difference.
levels.3: Explains that rivers flow and seas are large and salty, with a picture to show it.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 - Geography Curriculum!Fortnight 9-10: Water Bodies – Rivers and Seas; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Water tray flow
steps: Tilt a water tray gently.
Watch the water flow.
Talk about how a river flows.
Draw what you saw.

source.cell: Fortnight 9-10: Water Bodies – Rivers and Seas

levels.0: Says the water stays still when the tray is tilted and does not look again.
levels.1: Says the water moves only after the educator points to it.
levels.2: Describes how water flows in a tray like a river.
levels.3: Describes how a river differs from a sea using what they saw in the tray.

rows.name: Natural and man-made sorting
steps: Take a set of items.
Sort them into natural and man-made.
Match each natural item to its use.
Say one use of water.

levels.0: Puts a plastic cup with natural items and keeps it there after discussion.
levels.1: Sorts only water and soil and needs help for other items.
levels.2: Sorts natural and man-made items and names a use of one natural resource.
levels.3: Tells why people need water, air and soil with examples.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 - Geography Curriculum!Fortnight 11–12: Natural Resources; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Land use picture sort and map
steps: Look at pictures of farms, cities and roads.
Sort them into three groups.
Draw a simple map showing farm, city and road.
Point to a land use you see around school.

levels.0: Puts a road picture with the farms and does not move it when asked.
levels.1: Sorts only farms and houses and needs the educator for roads.
levels.2: Sorts pictures into farm, city and road and draws a simple land use map.
levels.3: Explains why land is used in different ways and names one land use near school.

rows.name: Draw a classroom map
steps: Look at the classroom from above in your mind.
Draw the door, desks and board as symbols.
Add a key for the symbols.
Find a place on a friend's map.

levels.0: Draws symbols with no key and cannot say what they mean.
levels.1: Draws the door and board only and needs the educator for desks.
levels.2: Draws a classroom map with symbols and a key.
levels.3: Finds a place on a friend's map and explains how they found it.
