rows.name: Treasure hunt using directions
steps: Hide a treasure in the classroom.
Write or say directions to it.
A partner follows them.
Check if the partner found it.

levels.0: Says left for right and the partner walks the wrong way.
levels.1: Follows directions only when the educator says each one slowly.
levels.2: Follows directions to find the hidden treasure.
levels.3: Gives directions that lead a partner to the treasure.

rows.note: named in Grade 2&3 - Geography Curriculum!Fortnight 15–17: Maps and Directions; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Line maze challenge
steps: Do a warm-up sketch using pencils on A4.
Look at the types of line (wavy, zigzag, dotted, thick, thin) on the board or slides.
Line maze challenge: draw a path using 4 or more types of line.
rows.materials: Chart of line types, sharpened pencils, black markers (A4 paper)

levels.0: Line maze path uses one or two kinds of line, or the wobbly lines cannot be told apart.
levels.1: Maze path shows four kinds of line only while the educator points to each one on the chart.
levels.2: Maze path shows wavy, zigzag, dotted, thick and thin lines, each clearly different from the next.
levels.3: Same line types appear again in a new drawing, such as a map, and the child names each aloud.

rows.name: Shape scavenger hunt and Shape Creature
steps: Do a shape scavenger hunt in the classroom, finding shapes in objects.
Create a collage using cut-outs of coloured paper shapes.
Arrange the shapes into an abstract 'Shape Creature'.

levels.0: Scavenger sheet shows no shapes drawn, or shapes are copied without a matching object.
levels.1: Hunt sheet has shapes drawn from objects only when the educator names the object to draw.
levels.2: Hunt sheet and creature show squares, circles and triangles plus a few curvy organic shapes drawn from real objects.
levels.3: Creature parts are labelled geometric or organic in the child's own words and a new object is added.

rows.name: Pattern play on grid paper
steps: Create repeating patterns on grid paper.
Use colour to enhance the pattern rhythm.
Add your square to the class pattern mural (collaborative).
rows.materials: Grid paper, colours (the document does not list materials)

levels.0: Grid squares show colours or shapes placed at random with no unit repeating.
levels.1: Pattern repeats on the grid for a few squares, then the unit changes or stops.
levels.2: Grid pattern repeats the same shape-and-line unit across the whole row with colour that follows the rhythm.
levels.3: Square for the class mural uses a new repeating unit and the child claps or reads the rhythm aloud.

rows.name: Cultural pattern painting (Warli or African prints)
steps: Look at simple Indian or African patterns shown by the educator.
Replicate one pattern on brown paper using white paint or crayons.
Show the finished work to a partner and say what was made.
rows.materials: Brown paper, white paint or crayons

levels.0: Pattern copy is missing the main motif, and the child cannot say where it comes from.
levels.1: Copied pattern is finished with the educator's prompts, and the country or art name is given when asked.
levels.2: Copied Warli or Ndebele-style pattern repeats its motif clearly and the child says which culture it is from.
levels.3: Points out the repeated motif and symmetry in a second cultural pattern and explains it unaided.

rows.note: named in G2-G3 Visual Arts Curriculum!Week 4: Pattern in Culture; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Pattern zoo: animal silhouettes
steps: Draw animal silhouettes.
Fill inside with different pattern zones.
Add a background in crayon resist (watercolour wash).
rows.materials: Not listed in the document (paper, crayons, watercolour)

levels.0: Animal outline is left empty or filled with one colour and no lines, shapes or pattern.
levels.1: Silhouette is filled with one pattern zone, and a second zone appears after the educator suggests it.
levels.2: Silhouette is filled in zones that each combine line, shape and pattern, with a wash behind that leaves the crayon showing.
levels.3: Pattern zoo animal silhouettes: the child draws a second silhouette in a new setting and says why each zone's pattern was chosen.

rows.name: Warm and cool colour abstract art
steps: Discuss sun and ice as metaphors for warm and cool.
Create abstract art using warm or cool tones.
Give the art a title (for example 'Fiery Night' or 'Cool Breeze').
rows.materials: Paint trays, brushes, mood word chart

levels.0: Painting mixes warm and cool colours at random, and the child names none as warm or cool.
levels.1: Painting keeps mostly warm or mostly cool colours once the educator sorts the paint pots first.
levels.2: Painting uses only reds, oranges and yellows or only blues, greens and purples, and the title matches the colours.
levels.3: Paints a second picture using the opposite group and says why the colours feel warm or cool.

rows.name: Mood Monsters
steps: Choose an emotion to show.
Create a monster using shapes and colours that match the emotion.
Show the finished work to a partner and say what was made.
rows.materials: Not listed in the document (paper, paints, crayons)

levels.0: Monster uses shapes and colours that do not seem to go with the idea it is meant to show.
levels.1: Monster shows the idea with colour only, and shapes are added after the educator asks about them.
levels.2: Monster's colours, jagged or round shapes and lines all fit one feeling, and the child can point to each.
levels.3: Mood Monsters: the child makes a second monster for a different feeling and explains how colour and shape changed.

rows.note: named in G2-G3 Visual Arts Curriculum!Week 9: Mood Monsters; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Starry Night layered sky

Create a layered sky using oil pastels and tissue collage.
Show the finished work to a partner and say what was made.
rows.materials: Not listed in the document (oil pastels, tissue paper)

source.cell: Week 10–11: Famous Artist Focus – Van Gogh's Starry Night

levels.0: Sky is flat with no swirls or layers, and the child cannot say how Van Gogh's painting was made.
levels.1: Sky has short strokes after the educator models them, and one stroke in Starry Night is pointed out.
levels.2: Sky shows swirling, thick strokes in layers of pastel and tissue, and the child describes the strokes seen in the painting.
levels.3: Starry Night layered sky: the child describes the strokes of a different painting aloud and uses them in a new night sky.

rows.name: Colour reflection and gallery walk
steps: Walk around the class display with reflection sheets.
Hold a peer discussion on a favourite artwork.
Reflect on the process and build art vocabulary.

levels.0: Reflection sheet stays blank, or no colour word is used when the child speaks about the artwork.
levels.1: Names one colour of own artwork only when the educator asks a question about it.

rows.name: The block bank: build a script on the table with cut-out cards
steps: Cut out the block cards and keep them in an envelope with your name on it.
Before you touch a computer, build your script on the table with the block cards.
Write the two blank cards in when the class meets blocks it has not seen yet.
rows.materials: Printed block bank sheet, scissors, named envelope

source.cell: Worksheet 11 – The block bank (Grades 2 and 3, cut and keep)

levels.0: Block cards lie in no order on the table, or a motion card sits first with no yellow event card above it.
levels.1: Lays out a card script only after the educator names the first card, such as when flag clicked.
levels.2: Cards on the table form a script that starts with an event card followed by motion blocks, which is then copied to the device.
levels.3: Swaps one card to change what the sprite does and tells a partner the new result in own words.

rows.note: Document gives the instruction as a short paragraph, not numbered steps. Shared with Grade 3.

rows.name: Predict, then run: read a script and say what it will do
steps: Do not touch the computer yet; read the script (when flag clicked, go to x: 0 y: 0, point in direction 90, move 100 steps, turn right 90 degrees, move 100 steps, say I am here! for 2 seconds).
Write what you think will happen and which way the sprite will be facing at the end.
Now run it and write what really happened; say if your prediction was right and, if not, which block surprised you.
Swap blocks 4 and 5 around and write what is different now.
rows.materials: Worksheet 12, a computer with Scratch or ScratchJr

levels.0: Writes a prediction that ignores the turn block, or leaves it blank and fills in only the result.
levels.1: Predicts the path only while the educator reads the blocks aloud, and cannot say why the result differed.
levels.2: Written prediction names the move, the turn and the say block, and the real result is written beside it.
levels.3: After swapping blocks 4 and 5, explains in own words why the order of blocks changes the final direction.

rows.note: Document notes that direction 90 means the sprite faces right.

rows.name: Draw the sprite's path from a script
steps: Follow the script with your pencil (go to x: -150 y: 0, point in direction 90, repeat 3 of move 100 steps, say step for 1 second, turn right 90 degrees, then move 100 steps) and draw the path the sprite takes on the stage.
Put an arrow where it ends, showing which way it is facing; one square is about 50 steps.
Answer: how many times does the sprite say step, how many blocks would you need without the repeat, and does it fall off the edge of the stage.
Now run it and check your drawing; write what you got wrong and why.
rows.materials: Worksheet 13 with stage grid, pencil, a computer with Scratch

levels.0: Path starts in the wrong place or ignores the repeat, and no arrow shows the facing direction at the end.
levels.1: Draws the first move and turn correctly but needs prompting to count the remaining loops and the last move.
levels.2: Drawn path shows three moves with turns from x of -150 and an end arrow, and the count of 'step' said is correct.
levels.3: Finds the mistake in own drawing after running the script and explains which block caused the difference.

rows.name: Write the script: the cat walks right, says hello and walks back
steps: Read what we want to happen: when the green flag is clicked the cat starts in the middle of the stage, walks to the right, waits, says hello, turns around, walks back to where it started, and stops.
Lay the blocks out on the table first, in order; when you are happy, write them on the sheet, one block per line.
Say which block makes it wait and how it will turn around; write your way.
Build it and run it; write how you know the cat went back to exactly where it started, and what you changed if it did not work the first time.
rows.materials: Worksheet 14, block bank cards, a computer with Scratch

levels.0: Blocks or list are out of order, so the cat walks back before saying hello or never returns to the start.
levels.1: Builds the walk right and the hello but needs help to find the wait block and the return move.
levels.2: Script starts with the flag, walks right, waits, says hello, turns and walks back, ending where the cat began.
levels.3: Writes a second way to turn around and extends the script so the cat goes round a square and back.

rows.note: Extension in the document: send the cat round a square and back.

rows.name: Change one thing: alter one block and say what will happen
steps: Take the script you built on Worksheet 14.
Change one block at a time; before each change write what you think will happen.
Run it and write what really happened in the table, one row for each change.
Say which change surprised you most, then add one thing nobody asked for and write what it is and why.
rows.materials: Worksheet 15, the Worksheet 14 script, a computer with Scratch

levels.0: Alters several blocks at once, so the table shows no clear link between a change and what happened.
levels.1: Changes one block per row but writes the expected effect only after running or after the educator asks.
levels.2: Table shows one block changed per row, a written guess before each run and the real result next to it.
levels.3: Adds an unrequested block, then tells a partner why it caused the surprise recorded in the table.

rows.note: Document gives the 'rule of one': change one thing, run it, write it down.

levels.1: Finds a device only with picture clues and says its name but not what it is used for.
levels.2: Drawing of the favourite tech item is labelled and the worksheet states one use of the device.
levels.3: Tells a partner how two different devices help people at school and why one is more useful.

rows.note: Document lists the activity and deliverable only; the three steps are the items in the table.

rows.name: Sequence picture cards and play Simon Says
steps: Educator asks: imagine you are teaching a robot to get ready for school; what would you tell it to do first?
Play Simon Says using the words first, then, next and last.
In groups, arrange mixed-up picture cards of an everyday task, such as brushing teeth, in the correct order and talk about the sequence.
Complete a similar sequencing worksheet on your own.
Play the verbal sequencing game: the educator calls out steps out of order and you correct the sequence by raising your hand and rearranging.
rows.materials: Printed sequencing cards (Brushing Teeth, Making a Sandwich), sequencing worksheet

levels.0: Cards stay mixed up, or 'last' is placed before 'first' in the sequence on the group's table.
levels.1: Orders the cards correctly in the group but the worksheet needs an educator hint for the middle steps.
levels.2: Worksheet shows the everyday task in the correct order, with first, next and last placed rightly.
levels.3: Spots a wrongly ordered step in the educator's spoken game and says which step should come before it.

rows.note: Planner also sets a peer checklist for accuracy and an optional online sequencing game.

rows.name: Debugging Relay Race: fix the wrong picture sequence
steps: Take a set of mixed-up picture cards that make a sequence with a mistake in it.
Find the card that is in the wrong place and move it so the sequence is correct, taking turns in the Debugging Relay Race.
Show the corrected sequence to another group so they can check it.

levels.0: Leaves the mixed-up card where it is, or moves a different card so the sequence still does not make sense.
levels.1: Fixes the sequence only after the educator points to the row where the mistake is.
levels.2: Moves the wrong card to its place so the picture sequence reads correctly from first to last.
levels.3: Explains which step was wrong and what would happen if the sequence ran as first given.

rows.name: Identify devices: cut-and-paste inputs and outputs
steps: Take the device cut-outs and the device identification sheet.
Cut out each device and paste it on the sheet where it belongs, as an input or an output.
Play the Device Identification Game and share your sheet with a partner to check.
rows.materials: Device cut-outs, device identification sheet, scissors, glue

levels.0: Pastes the keyboard or the screen in the wrong group, or leaves device cut-outs unpasted.
levels.1: Pastes obvious devices correctly but needs a hint for devices that do both, like a touch screen.
levels.2: Identification sheet shows every cut-out pasted under input or output, with an example named for each.
levels.3: Names a new device from the classroom and says what goes in and what comes out, unprompted.

rows.note: named in G2-3 Cambridge_Primary_Computing_Curriculum.xlsx!Detailed Planner – Month 1, Week 3 (Grade 2 Activity); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Loop Dance Game with loop cards
steps: Take the loop instruction cards and make up dance steps.
Write a dance step with a loop card that says how many times to repeat it.
Dance the steps, repeating each one as many times as its loop card says, and let a partner check the count.

levels.0: Writes the same dance step on several cards in a row and never uses a loop card.
levels.1: Uses a loop card but the number on it does not match the repeats danced, until prompted.
levels.2: Dance shows each step repeated exactly the number written on its loop card.
levels.3: Replaces a long list of repeated steps with loop cards and tells peers why the dance stays the same.

rows.note: named in G2-3 Cambridge_Primary_Computing_Curriculum.xlsx!Detailed Planner – Month 1, Week 4 (Grade 2 Activity); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: ScratchJr guided project with a storyboard
steps: Draw a storyboard of your ScratchJr project on paper.
Follow the guided steps in ScratchJr to make your sprite move as drawn in the storyboard.
Play your initial project and show it to a partner.

levels.0: Storyboard is blank or the ScratchJr screen shows blocks lying unconnected, so the sprite does not move.
levels.1: Builds the first move from the storyboard only with step-by-step guidance from the educator or a partner.
levels.2: Snapped blocks make the sprite perform the move drawn in the storyboard when the project is played.
levels.3: Adds a second move that is not in the storyboard and tells how the blocks changed to produce it.

rows.note: named in G2-3 Cambridge_Primary_Computing_Curriculum.xlsx!Detailed Planner – Month 2, Week 5 (Grade 2 Activity); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Debugging Challenge: debug a ScratchJr project
steps: Open the ScratchJr project that does not work.
Find which block is wrong or missing, fix it and play the project again.
Take a screenshot of the debugged project to submit.

levels.0: Replays the project and the same fault remains, with no block pointed out as the cause.
levels.1: Finds the faulty block only when the educator narrows it to one script.
levels.2: Screenshot submitted shows the corrected script working, with the faulty block replaced or reconnected.
levels.3: Explains how the fault was found by testing block by block and finds a second fault alone.

rows.note: named in G2-3 Cambridge_Primary_Computing_Curriculum.xlsx!Detailed Planner – Month 2, Week 7 (Grade 2 Activity); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Micro:bit Guessing Game: explore inputs and outputs
steps: Explore the micro:bit kit and look at its buttons and its LED display.
Play the Micro:bit Guessing Game about the inputs and outputs you find.
Write your micro:bit exploration notes: which parts are inputs and which are outputs.

levels.0: Notes list micro:bit parts but name no input or output, or place the buttons under output.
levels.1: Names the buttons as input after the educator presses one and asks what the micro:bit did.
levels.2: Exploration notes name the buttons as inputs and the LED display as output, and say what each does.
levels.3: Predicts what the LEDs will show for a new button press and checks the guess on the micro:bit.

rows.name: Data Sorting Game with printed data sets
steps: Take the printed data set.
Play the Data Sorting Game: sort the data into groups.
Complete the data analysis worksheet by writing what the data shows.
rows.materials: Printed data sets, data analysis worksheet

levels.0: Sorts data cards into groups that share no feature, and the worksheet states no pattern.
levels.1: Sorts the printed data but names a pattern only after the educator asks which group is biggest.
levels.2: Worksheet states one pattern seen in the table, such as which group has most, using the printed data.
levels.3: Shows how the pattern could help a decision at school and spots a row that breaks it.

rows.note: Planner gives 'Understand how data is useful' and the game name; the rules of the game are not given.

rows.name: Spreadsheet Puzzle: make a basic spreadsheet
steps: Open the spreadsheet software on the computer.
Type the given data into rows and columns to create a basic spreadsheet.
Take part in the Spreadsheet Puzzle and check your entries for accuracy.

levels.0: Types the data in one long line or in cells with no row and column pattern.
levels.1: Places data in cells correctly only after being shown which column each kind of item belongs in.
levels.2: Spreadsheet shows each item in its own row with its value in the next column, without typing errors.
levels.3: Adds a new row and column of own choice and explains what each column holds.

rows.note: Planner gives 'Create basic spreadsheets' and the game name; the puzzle rules are not given.

rows.name: Chart Building Race: make a simple chart
steps: Start from a table of data on the computer.
Make a simple chart from the data in the Chart Building Race.
Present your chart to the class.

levels.0: Chart bars do not match the numbers in the data table, or the chart has no labels.
levels.1: Builds the chart only with the educator's help to choose which columns to use.
levels.2: Chart on screen shows each data item as a bar whose size matches the table, with a title.
levels.3: Tells the class what the chart shows and which item is biggest, then changes one number to show the chart change.

rows.note: named in G2-3 Cambridge_Primary_Computing_Curriculum.xlsx!Detailed Planner – Month 4, Week 15 (Grade 2 Activity); some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: I/O Scavenger Hunt in the classroom
steps: Take the classroom device checklist and walk around the classroom.
Find each device and mark whether it is an input or an output.
Fill in the input/output identification sheet and share it with a partner.
rows.materials: Classroom device checklist, input/output identification sheet

levels.0: Lists classroom objects that are not devices, or marks a speaker as an input.
levels.1: Finds devices on the checklist but needs the educator to say whether each one is input or output.
levels.2: Identification sheet lists at least one classroom device marked input and one marked output correctly.
levels.3: Finds a device that is both input and output, such as a touch screen, and explains why.

rows.name: संयुक्ताक्षर पहेली – टूटे भागों से शब्द बनाओ
steps: संयुक्ताक्षर वाले शब्दों के टूटे हुए भागों के कार्ड लो।
भागों को जोड़कर पूरा शब्द बनाओ।
बना हुआ शब्द ज़ोर से पढ़ो और साथी से जाँच करवाओ।
rows.materials: Word cards broken into parts (words with क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ, श्र)

source.cell: 6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – June: Fun Project / Activity

levels.0: Joins parts into a non-word, or reads क्ष as क and leaves out the conjunct sound.
levels.1: Builds the word with a partner's hint and reads the conjunct only after the educator says it first.
levels.2: Assembled word card is whole and correct, and the conjunct क्ष, त्र or ज्ञ is read aloud clearly.
levels.3: Builds a new word with श्र or ज्ञ that is not on the cards and reads it to the group.

rows.note: named in Hindi_Curriculum_Grades_1-4.docx!6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – June: Fun Project / Activity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: संज्ञा छँटाई खेल – चित्र-कार्ड
steps: चित्र-कार्ड लो और हर चित्र का नाम बोलो।
हर कार्ड को व्यक्ति, स्थान या वस्तु के समूह में रखो।
साथी के समूह देखो और बताओ कि कोई कार्ड बदलना है या नहीं।

source.cell: 6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – July: Fun Project / Activity

levels.0: Puts a picture of a school in the person group, or says no naming word for the cards.
levels.1: Sorts most cards correctly but needs the educator's hint for place words such as बाज़ार.
levels.2: Picture cards sit in the right person, place or thing group and the naming word is said for each.
levels.3: Brings a new example for each group from the classroom and explains why it fits.

rows.note: named in Hindi_Curriculum_Grades_1-4.docx!6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – July: Fun Project / Activity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: ‘एक से अनेक’ फ्लैशकार्ड फ्लिप खेल
steps: एकवचन शब्द वाला फ्लैशकार्ड उठाओ।
कार्ड पलटने से पहले उसका बहुवचन बोलो।
कार्ड पलटकर जाँचो कि तुम्हारा उत्तर सही है या नहीं।
rows.materials: Flashcards with singular words (एकवचन) and plural words (बहुवचन) on the back

source.cell: 6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – August: Fun Project / Activity

levels.0: Repeats the singular word or adds a wrong ending, so the plural spoken does not match the card.
levels.1: Gives plurals for common words but needs the card flipped first for words like बच्चा.
levels.2: Says the correct plural for each flashcard before flipping it, and the flipped side agrees.
levels.3: Uses the plural in a spoken sentence and explains the change in own words.

rows.note: named in Hindi_Curriculum_Grades_1-4.docx!6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – August: Fun Project / Activity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: वाक्य-पट्टी खेल – शब्द-कार्ड लगाओ
steps: शब्द-कार्ड की पट्टियाँ लो जिनसे चार-पाँच शब्द का वाक्य बन सकता है।
कार्डों को सही क्रम में लगाकर पूरा वाक्य बनाओ।
वाक्य ज़ोर से पढ़ो और साथी से जाँच करवाओ।
rows.materials: Word-card strips for 4 to 5 word sentences

source.cell: 6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – September: Fun Project / Activity

levels.0: Lays cards in any order and the sentence read out makes no sense.
levels.1: Builds a four-word sentence but needs a hint about where the action word goes.
levels.2: Word strips form a four or five word sentence in the correct order, read aloud once.
levels.3: Rearranges the same cards into a second sentence with a different meaning and reads both.

rows.note: named in Hindi_Curriculum_Grades_1-4.docx!6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – September: Fun Project / Activity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: दीवाली ग्रीटिंग कार्ड लेखन
steps: दीवाली से जुड़े शब्द सोचो और बोर्ड पर लिखे शब्द देखो।
ग्रीटिंग कार्ड पर दीवाली का एक शुभकामना वाक्य हिंदी में लिखो।
कार्ड सजाओ और साथी को पढ़कर सुनाओ।
rows.materials: Card paper, colours, festival word list

source.cell: 6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – October: Fun Project / Activity

levels.0: Card has a drawing but no Hindi greeting, or the festival words are copied wrongly from the board.
levels.1: Writes the greeting only by copying a model from the board, with matras checked by the educator.
levels.2: Card holds a written Hindi festival greeting with at least one festival word spelled correctly.
levels.3: Writes a greeting using two festival words of own choice and reads it aloud to a classmate.

rows.note: named in Hindi_Curriculum_Grades_1-4.docx!6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – October: Fun Project / Activity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: विलोम शब्द मेमोरी-मैच खेल
steps: विलोम शब्दों के कार्ड उल्टे रखो।
दो कार्ड पलटो; अगर दोनों शब्द विलोम हैं तो जोड़ी रख लो, नहीं तो वापस उल्टे रख दो।
अपनी जोड़ियाँ बोलकर सुनाओ और साथी से जाँच करवाओ।
rows.materials: Memory-match cards with 8 pairs of opposite words

source.cell: 6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – November: Fun Project / Activity

levels.0: Turns up two cards and keeps them as a pair although the words are not opposites.
levels.1: Matches familiar pairs like ऊपर–नीचे but needs the educator's hint for the other pairs.
levels.2: Keeps correct opposite pairs from the eight pairs and says both words of each pair aloud.
levels.3: Gives a new opposite not on the cards and uses the pair in a spoken sentence.

rows.note: named in Hindi_Curriculum_Grades_1-4.docx!6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – November: Fun Project / Activity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: मेरा स्कूल का दिन – छोटा अनुच्छेद और चित्र
steps: स्कूल की एक गतिविधि चुनो जो तुमने की है।
उस गतिविधि के बारे में दो-तीन पंक्तियों का अनुच्छेद हिंदी में लिखो।
अपने अनुच्छेद के साथ चित्र बनाओ और साथी को पढ़कर सुनाओ।

source.cell: 6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – December: Fun Project / Activity

levels.0: Writes one word or a list instead of connected lines, and the drawing has no link to the text.
levels.1: Writes two lines with the educator's sentence starters and a drawing that matches.
levels.2: Paragraph has two or three connected Hindi lines about a school activity beside a matching drawing.
levels.3: Adds a closing line of own idea and reads the paragraph aloud to the group with the drawing.

rows.note: named in Hindi_Curriculum_Grades_1-4.docx!6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – December: Fun Project / Activity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: पर्यायवाची बिंगो
steps: बिंगो कार्ड लो जिस पर पर्यायवाची शब्द लिखे हैं।
जब educator कोई शब्द बोले, तो उसके समान अर्थ वाला शब्द अपने कार्ड पर ढूँढकर निशान लगाओ।
एक पंक्ति पूरी होने पर ‘बिंगो’ बोलो और अपने जोड़े ज़ोर से पढ़ो।
rows.materials: Bingo cards with synonym words (5 to 6 common pairs)

source.cell: 6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – January: Fun Project / Activity

levels.0: Marks a word on the card that does not share meaning with the word called.
levels.1: Marks a match only after hearing the educator say the meaning of the called word.
levels.2: Marks the correct same-meaning word for each called word and says the pair aloud.
levels.3: Says a synonym for a called word that is not on the card and uses it in a sentence.

rows.note: named in Hindi_Curriculum_Grades_1-4.docx!6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – January: Fun Project / Activity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: हाव-भाव के साथ कविता पाठ
steps: कक्षा की एक कविता चुनो और उसे कई बार पढ़कर याद करो।
हर पंक्ति के साथ एक हाव-भाव या क्रिया सोचो।
कक्षा के सामने कविता क्रिया के साथ सुनाओ।

source.cell: 6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – February: Fun Project / Activity

levels.0: Stops partway through the poem or recites with no actions, looking at the floor throughout.
levels.1: Recites the poem only while the educator or group says the first word of each line.
levels.2: Recites the whole poem aloud with an action that matches each line.
levels.3: Recites with changing voice and pauses at line ends, and teaches a classmate one action.

rows.note: named in Hindi_Curriculum_Grades_1-4.docx!6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – February: Fun Project / Activity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: हिंदी मेला – पढ़ने वाला दोस्त (कक्षा 1 के साथ)
steps: अपने साल के सीखने का कोई एक छोटा पाठ या काम हिंदी मेले के स्टॉल के लिए तैयार करो।
कक्षा 1 के पढ़ने वाले दोस्त को वह पाठ ज़ोर से पढ़कर सुनाओ।
दोस्त से एक सवाल पूछो और उसका उत्तर सुनो।
rows.materials: Hindi Mela stall display, a short text to read

source.cell: 6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – March: Fun Project / Activity

levels.0: Reads so quietly or fast that the Grade 1 buddy cannot follow, and skips lines.
levels.1: Reads to the buddy only with the educator pointing to each word.
levels.2: Reads the chosen text aloud to the buddy, at a pace the buddy can follow.
levels.3: Pauses to ask the buddy a question about the text and points to each word read.

rows.note: named in Hindi_Curriculum_Grades_1-4.docx!6. Grade 2 Month-by-Month Plan – March: Fun Project / Activity; some steps were added by the worker

rows.name: Write a story about a big brother or sister
steps: Read one of the unit stories, such as 'Younger Brother', and talk about what happens between a brother and a sister.
Plan the story aloud with a partner: who is in it, where it happens and what goes wrong.
Write the story in sentences with a beginning, a middle and an end.
Read the story aloud to a partner and add one more detail.
rows.materials: Story books from the unit, writing notebook

levels.0: Writing is a few separate sentences with no clear order, so the story has no beginning or ending.
levels.1: With a prompt for each part, sentences cover a beginning and a problem but stop before an ending.
levels.2: The story has a beginning, a middle and an ending written in connected sentences about a brother or sister.
levels.3: The story adds a detail or conversation that makes the problem and its fix clear to a reader who has not heard the plan.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B4

rows.name: Write a poem about things a friend or family member says
steps: Read 'The Things Mum Say' and pick out the lines that repeat what a family member says.
List three things a friend or someone at home often says.
Write a short poem using those sayings, with a repeating line.
Read the poem aloud to the group.

levels.0: Poem is a list of words with no repeated or spoken line from anyone.
levels.1: Poem has one saying written down after the educator gives an example line.
levels.2: Poem uses three sayings in short lines and repeats one line.
levels.3: Poem repeats a saying in a pattern and the reading aloud changes voice for each speaker.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B4

rows.name: Write a funny family story
steps: Share a funny thing that could happen at home and choose one to write about.
Make a three-box plan: start, funny moment, end.
Write the story using at least one conversation line.
Swap with a partner, read it and tell the funniest part.

levels.0: Writing lists events with no funny moment and no order.
levels.1: The funny moment is written but the start or the end is missing.
levels.2: Start, funny moment and end are all written and a conversation line is included.
levels.3: The funny moment is built up over several sentences and the partner can say why it is funny.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B4

rows.name: Present a show and tell item
steps: Choose one item from home that tells about the family or a friend.
Practise saying three sentences about it: what it is, where it came from, why it matters.
Hold the item up and speak to the group in a clear voice.
Answer one question from a listener.

levels.0: Item is held up but nothing is said, or the voice cannot be heard at the back.
levels.1: Says one sentence about the item with prompting questions from the educator.
levels.2: Says three clear sentences about the item and answers a question.
levels.3: Speaks with the item shown, in order, and answers two questions with a reason.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B4

rows.name: Read speech aloud in character using speech marks
steps: Find the speech marks in a short story and underline what each character says.
Choose a character and practise the lines in a voice that suits them.
Read the story in a group, with one reader for each character and one for the narrator.
Talk about how the voices changed the story.

levels.0: Lines are read in one flat voice and the speech marks are not used to tell who is speaking.
levels.1: Reads own character's lines in the right place after the educator points to them.
levels.2: Reads own lines in a voice for the character and stops at the speech marks.
levels.3: Changes voice for each character and corrects a partner who reads narration as speech.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B4

rows.name: Write instructions for a science experiment
steps: Read 'How to mix oil + water' and point to the numbered steps.
Do a small experiment with the group, such as mixing oil and water.
Write the steps in order, each starting with a command word.
Swap with a partner who follows the steps to check they work.

levels.0: Writing tells what happened rather than what to do, with no steps in order.
levels.1: Steps are numbered but some do not begin with a command word.
levels.2: Every step starts with a command word and a partner can follow them in order.
levels.3: Steps include what to use and a warning, and a partner repeats the experiment without asking for help.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B6

rows.name: Write a flowchart for following instructions
steps: Look at the flowchart 'How to blow bubbles' and name what the arrows show.
Pick a simple task such as washing hands and list its steps.
Draw a flowchart with boxes and arrows in the right order.
Show it to a partner who follows the arrows.

levels.0: Boxes are drawn without arrows, so the order cannot be followed.
levels.1: Arrows join the boxes after the educator reminds the order of the first two steps.
levels.2: Boxes and arrows show every step in order and a partner can follow them.
levels.3: Flowchart adds a yes or no choice box and the partner follows both ways.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B6

rows.name: Present a badge pathway
steps: Read 'How to plan a Badge Pathway' and talk about badges the class could earn.
Plan a pathway of three badges on a chart with what to do for each.
Practise saying the pathway in order.
Present the pathway to the group and take one question.

levels.0: Chart has badge names but no steps to earn them and nothing is said in order.
levels.1: Pathway has two steps and is explained only when the educator asks about each box.
levels.2: Three steps are on the chart and are explained in order to the group.
levels.3: Pathway is explained with reasons for the order and one question is answered with an example.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B6

rows.name: Write an information text
steps: Read a short information text and find the title, headings and facts.
Gather three facts about a chosen topic from the unit.
Write a title and a short paragraph for each fact.
Read it to a partner and add one missing fact.

levels.0: Writing is one long line of facts with no title or headings.
levels.1: A title is added and facts are in separate lines after the educator models one.
levels.2: Title, headings and one paragraph for each of three facts are written.
levels.3: Facts are grouped under headings in order and a missing fact is spotted and added.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B6

rows.name: Read tongue twisters aloud
steps: Read 'She sells seashells', 'Betty Botter' and 'Peter Piper' together slowly.
Clap the beats and repeat each line three times.
Try a twister at speed with a partner and count mistakes.
Say a favourite twister to the group.

levels.0: Words are skipped or mixed up even when read slowly.
levels.1: Reads a twister slowly, stumbling twice at speed.
levels.2: Says a twister without stumbling after practice.
levels.3: Says two twisters fast and clearly and explains which sound repeats.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B16

rows.name: Write a chant
steps: Listen to a chant and clap its beat.
Choose a topic and list words that rhyme with it.
Write four lines with a steady beat and a rhyming word at each line end.
Practise the chant with a clap or stamp.

levels.0: Lines are written with no rhyme and do not fit a beat.
levels.1: Two lines rhyme after the educator suggests the second rhyming word.
levels.2: Four lines have a steady beat and end in rhyming words.
levels.3: The chant keeps its beat and adds a repeating line the group can join.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B16

rows.name: Perform a chant in a group
steps: Choose a class chant and share the lines among the group.
Add actions or claps to each line.
Practise until all voices start and stop together.
Perform for another group.

levels.0: Voices start at different times and the lines cannot be followed.
levels.1: Starts together after a count from the educator but loses the beat mid-way.
levels.2: The group keeps one beat and every child says their lines clearly.
levels.3: The group adds actions that match the words and keeps time without the educator counting.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B17

rows.name: Act out a rhyme in a group
steps: Read a short rhyme and decide who or what each part is.
Give each child a line and an action.
Practise the rhyme with the actions.
Perform it for the class.

levels.0: Actions do not match the lines being said.
levels.1: Acts the line after the educator points to it.
levels.2: Says the line and acts it at the right time.
levels.3: Acts and speaks with the other children without prompts and adds a small detail of their own.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B17

rows.name: Write a poem using a rhyming pattern
steps: Read 'New Shoes' and find the rhyming words at line ends.
Choose a topic and list rhyming word pairs.
Write four lines that follow the same rhyme pattern.
Read the poem aloud and underline the rhymes.

levels.0: Lines are written with no rhyming words at the ends.
levels.1: One pair of lines rhymes when rhyme pairs are listed first.
levels.2: Four lines rhyme in a set pattern and the rhymes are underlined.
levels.3: The poem keeps its pattern across a second verse.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B17

rows.name: Talk about the sequence of a story
steps: Read 'Yoshi the Stonecutter' together.
Put picture cards of the story events on the floor in a muddle.
Place them in order and say what happened first, next and last.
Check the order against the book.

levels.0: Events are placed with no order and the story cannot be told from them.
levels.1: Places three events in order after help with the first.
levels.2: Puts the cards in the right order and says first, next, last.
levels.3: Orders the events and explains why one event had to come before another.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B27

rows.name: Listen to an explanation text and answer questions
steps: Listen to the text 'What is a Drone?' read aloud.
Ask who, what, why and how questions about it.
Answer in a full sentence and point to the part of the text that tells.
Listen to a partner's answer and add one fact.

levels.0: Answers do not match the questions asked.
levels.1: Answers a who or what question when the educator repeats it.
levels.2: Answers each question in a sentence that matches the text.
levels.3: Answers and shows where in the text the answer is found, then adds a fact from a partner's answer.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B28

rows.name: Discuss the moral of a story
steps: Read 'Sorry Isn't Good Enough', 'Little Albatross' or 'The Best Tailor in Pinbau'.
Name the characters and the problem.
Say how the problem was solved.
Talk about what the story teaches.

levels.0: Characters are named but the problem and the ending are not told.
levels.1: Names the problem and the fix after questions from the educator.
levels.2: Names the characters, the problem and the fix and says what the story teaches.
levels.3: Compares the lesson with another story read earlier.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B43

rows.name: Discuss fish body parts and what they do
steps: Look at a labelled fish diagram and read the captions.
Name each body part and say what it does.
Match name cards to the parts on the diagram.
Share one fact with the group.

levels.0: Parts are named without saying what they do.
levels.1: Names three parts and says what one does with help.
levels.2: Names the parts and says the job of each from the captions.
levels.3: Uses new words such as camouflage and habitat to explain how one part helps the fish live.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!B49

rows.name: Count up to 100 objects and write the number names
steps: Count out objects in tens using counters and a Ganit Mala up to 100.
Say the number aloud as each ten is added.
Write the number in digits and in words.
Check the count with a partner.

levels.0: Counting skips or repeats numbers so the total changes on a second count.
levels.1: Counts in tens with help and writes the number in digits only.
levels.2: Counts up to 100 objects correctly and writes the number in digits and words.
levels.3: Counts a large pile by grouping and writes number names for any number to 100 without a chart.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C4

rows.name: Problem of the Month
steps: Read the month's problem aloud and say what is asked.
Draw or use counters to try a way to solve it.
Share the way with a partner and compare answers.
Tell the class how the group solved it.

levels.0: Starts without saying what the problem asks and gives an answer with no working.
levels.1: Tries a drawing but needs the educator to say what to do next.
levels.2: Solves with a drawing or counters and explains the way used.
levels.3: Solves by a second way and explains why both give the same answer.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C4

rows.name: Revise counting in 2s, 5s and 10s and the tables of 2, 5 and 10
steps: Count in 2s, 5s and 10s along a number line.
Chant each table together and say it without the line.
Play a quick-fire round where a partner calls a fact.
Write each table from memory.

levels.0: Counts in ones or loses the step after a few numbers.
levels.1: Counts in 2s, 5s and 10s with the number line in view.
levels.2: Counts in steps and says the 2, 5 and 10 table facts without counting up.
levels.3: Says the three tables in any order and links the 10s to the 5s.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C4

rows.name: Word problems and MCQ-pattern practice
steps: Read a word problem and underline the key words.
Choose add, subtract or multiply.
Pick the correct answer from four choices after working it out.
Check each answer by estimating.

levels.0: Picks an answer without working or checking.
levels.1: Chooses the operation after the educator names the key word.
levels.2: Chooses the operation, works it out and ticks the matching choice.
levels.3: Spots a wrong choice by estimating before working and explains the check.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C23

rows.name: Sketch the reflection of a 2D shape
steps: Draw a shape on squared paper next to a line.
Count squares from each corner to the line.
Mark the same distance on the other side and join the points.
Check with a mirror.

levels.0: Shape is drawn on the other side but flipped the wrong way.
levels.1: Reflection is correct for two corners when squares are counted aloud.
levels.2: Reflection is drawn correctly and checked with a mirror.
levels.3: Reflects a shape across a slanted line or explains what changed and what stayed the same.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C27

rows.name: Describe movements using position and movement words
steps: Place a toy on a grid and give a move such as 'two squares left'.
A partner moves the toy.
Swap and give a move with a turn word.
Write a short route on paper.

levels.0: Moves are given without direction words and the toy ends up elsewhere.
levels.1: Gives one direction word correctly and needs a prompt for the distance.
levels.2: Gives a route with direction words and distances that a partner can follow.
levels.3: Writes a route with a turn and checks a partner's moves against it.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C27

rows.name: Solve multiplication word problems with one-digit numbers
steps: Read the problem and draw equal groups.
Write the number sentence.
Solve and write the answer in a sentence.
Make up a problem for a partner.

levels.0: Draws unequal groups and adds the wrong numbers.
levels.1: Draws equal groups and solves when the number sentence is given.
levels.2: Draws groups, writes the number sentence and answers in a sentence.
levels.3: Writes a new problem and the matching number sentence.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C27

rows.name: Predict how many times a shape looks the same in a full turn
steps: Cut out a shape and mark one corner.
Predict how many times it looks the same in a full turn.
Turn it a quarter at a time and count.
Compare with the prediction.

levels.0: Turns are counted without a mark so the count is unclear.
levels.1: Counts turns of a square when the corner is marked.
levels.2: Predicts and checks the count for two shapes.
levels.3: Explains why the count changes for another shape.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C28

rows.name: Use a folded circle to find angles and turns
steps: Fold a paper circle in half twice to find the centre.
Mark quarter, half and full turns.
Turn a pointer to each mark.
Name each turn.

levels.0: Folds do not meet at one centre.
levels.1: Finds the centre after a demonstration and names the full turn.
levels.2: Finds the centre and names quarter, half and full turns.
levels.3: Describes a turn between the marks.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C37

rows.name: Describe regular and random patterns
steps: Look at a set of patterns on cards.
Sort them into regular and random.
Say how you know.
Make a new pattern of each kind.

levels.0: Patterns are put in one pile without a reason.
levels.1: Sorts them when the educator names the pattern rule.
levels.2: Sorts into regular and random and says what repeats.
levels.3: Makes both kinds and explains the repeat.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C37

rows.name: Find connections between the 1x, 2x, 5x and 10x tables
steps: Write the 1x, 2x, 5x and 10x tables side by side.
Look for facts that link, such as double and half.
Use the links to work out a new fact.
Tell a partner the link.

levels.0: Tables are copied with no link noticed.
levels.1: Sees that 10x is double 5x when shown one example.
levels.2: Finds links between the four tables and uses one to find a fact.
levels.3: Uses links to find a fact from a table not yet learned.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C43

rows.name: Check that both sides of an equals sign have the same value
steps: Write number sentences with an equals sign.
Work out the left and then the right side.
Say if the two values are the same.
Change one number to make them equal.

levels.0: Only the left side is worked out and the answer is written after the sign.
levels.1: Works both sides but cannot say if they match.
levels.2: Works out both sides and says whether they are equal.
levels.3: Changes a number to make an unbalanced sentence equal.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!C43

rows.name: Soil in a tray: look closely and draw
steps: Place soil in a tray with a plant and a magnifying lens.
Look at the soil and say where soil is seen and what is in it.
Draw what you see with colour pencils.
Wash hands and share one thing found in the soil.
rows.materials: Soil tray, plant, magnifying lens, paper, colour pencils

levels.0: Drawing shows a brown patch with no parts of the soil.
levels.1: Draws one thing found in the soil after the educator points to it.
levels.2: Draws several parts seen with the lens, such as stones and roots.
levels.3: Labels the parts and says what they are made from.

rows.note: Next steps tab: soil lesson, Period 1.

rows.name: Test two types of soil with water
steps: Place two kinds of soil in separate bowls.
Pour the same amount of water on each.
Look closely and draw what happens.
Say which soil held more water.
rows.materials: Two soil types, water bowl, magnifying glass, paper

levels.0: Water is poured on one bowl only.
levels.1: Pours water on both and describes one change.
levels.2: Pours the same water on both and says which held more.
levels.3: Gives a reason for the difference and predicts a third soil.

rows.note: Next steps tab: soil lesson, Period 2.

rows.name: Compare plants and animals in different habitats
steps: Look at pictures of a pond, a desert and a forest.
Name a plant and an animal in each.
Sort picture cards into the right habitat.
Say why an animal lives there.

levels.0: Cards are placed with no link to the pictures.
levels.1: Places cards in the right habitat after hints.
levels.2: Names a plant and an animal for each habitat.
levels.3: Says why one animal could not live in another habitat.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!E4

rows.name: Explore forces that change shape, speed and direction
steps: Squash clay and say what changed.
Push a toy car gently and then harder.
Push a ball against a wall.
Tell which change was caused by the push.

levels.0: Objects are moved but the change is not described.
levels.1: Describes one change after the educator asks.
levels.2: Shows a push changing shape, speed and direction.
levels.3: Predicts what a harder push will do and tests it.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!E11

rows.name: Poster to help save planet Earth
steps: Talk about ways to look after the planet.
Pick one way and draw it.
Write a sentence under the picture.
Show the poster and tell the group.

levels.0: Poster has a picture and no message.
levels.1: Picture and a short word are added after help.
levels.2: Poster has a picture and a clear sentence.
levels.3: Poster explains why the action helps and gives a second way.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!E16

rows.name: Sort waste: trash vs compost
steps: Look at pictures or real waste items.
Sort into two baskets: compost or trash.
Check with a partner.
Say what compost becomes.

levels.0: Items are placed in either basket without a reason.
levels.1: Sorts most items after one is modelled.
levels.2: Sorts waste into compost and trash and says why.
levels.3: Explains why a compost item can become soil.

rows.name: Workbook challenges: transparent, translucent and opaque
steps: Test objects with a torch.
Sort them as transparent, translucent or opaque.
Fill in the workbook table.
Talk about one surprising object.

levels.0: Objects are sorted by colour instead of how much light passes.
levels.1: Sorts clear and solid objects but mixes up translucent ones.
levels.2: Sorts objects into all three groups after testing.
levels.3: Predicts for a new object and tests.

rows.note: Activity name from the educators' daily log.

rows.name: Soluble and insoluble: revise with a workbook activity
steps: Stir salt and sand in water.
See what dissolves.
Record in a table.
Do the workbook page.

levels.0: Items are stirred but not recorded.
levels.1: Records one result with help.
levels.2: Records which dissolved and which did not.
levels.3: Predicts and tests a new material.

rows.note: Activity name from the educators' daily log.

rows.name: Make bhel
steps: Wash hands and read the safety rules.
Wash and cut the vegetables with help.
Mix the ingredients in a bowl.
Serve and taste.

levels.0: Washing or mixing is skipped and tools are not used safely.
levels.1: Mixes the bhel with each step shown by the educator.
levels.2: Washes, cuts safely and mixes bhel following the steps.
levels.3: Explains why each step was done and suggests a change.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!E11

rows.name: Paper plate bowl weaving
steps: Cut slits around a paper plate.
Weave strips over and under.
Tuck the ends in.
Show the bowl.

levels.0: Strips are pushed through at random.
levels.1: Weaves two rows over-under with help.
levels.2: Weaves the whole plate over and under.
levels.3: Makes a pattern by changing colours.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!E23

rows.name: Learn the 28 states and capitals on a map of India
steps: Look at a political map of India.
Find your own state and its capital.
Match state and capital cards.
Say five pairs.

levels.0: Capitals are matched to states at random.
levels.1: Matches five states and capitals with the map.
levels.2: Names the state and capital for several states.
levels.3: Locates a state and capital from the name alone.

rows.name: Learn countries of Asia, Europe and the Americas on a map
steps: Look at a world map and find the continent.
Name three countries in it.
Find them on a map puzzle.
Say one fact about one country.

levels.0: Countries are named without finding them on the map.
levels.1: Finds a country when shown its name.
levels.2: Names three countries of a continent and finds them.
levels.3: Compares two continents.

rows.note: Cells list 'Asian and European countries' and 'North and South American'.

rows.name: Play the seven notes on a keyboard
steps: Look at the seven notes on a keyboard.
Play them up and down.
Play a simple alankar.
Play along with a partner.

levels.0: Keys are pressed at random with no order.
levels.1: Plays notes up with help.
levels.2: Plays the seven notes in order.
levels.3: Plays alankars in order.

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!F37

rows.name: Claude Monet introduction class
steps: Look at a Monet painting.
Say what colours and strokes are seen.
Make a quick sketch in the style.
Tell what they notice.

levels.0: Looks at the painting without saying what is seen.
levels.1: Names one colour when asked.
levels.2: Describes colours and brush marks.
levels.3: Compares two paintings.

rows.note: Activity name from the educators' log.

rows.name: Knife painting
steps: Squeeze paint onto a paper plate.
Spread with a plastic knife.
Layer colours.
Describe the picture.

levels.0: Paint is mixed to brown.
levels.1: Spreads one colour.
levels.2: Layers two colours.
levels.3: Describes the effect.

rows.note: Activity name from the educators' log.

rows.name: Wall mural
steps: Pick a theme as a group.
Divide the wall.
Paint a part.
Look at the whole mural.

levels.0: Paints one area with no link to the theme.
levels.1: Paints a part with direction.
levels.2: Paints a part that fits the theme.
levels.3: Joins two parts.

rows.note: Activity name from the educators' log.

rows.name: Sikku kolam and kite making
steps: See a sikku kolam.
Draw dots and join them.
Make a kite pattern.
Show it.

levels.0: Lines do not follow the dots.
levels.1: Joins dots with help.
levels.2: Draws a pattern with dots and lines.
levels.3: Makes a kite with the pattern.

rows.note: Activity name from the educators' log.

rows.name: Pencil sketching: light and shadow
steps: Look at an object in light.
Draw its outline.
Shade the dark side.
Compare with a partner.

levels.0: Shading covers the whole drawing evenly.
levels.1: Shades one side.
levels.2: Shades dark to light.
levels.3: Explains where the light comes from.

rows.note: Activity name from the educators' log.

rows.name: अपना परिचय: बोलना और अपना नाम लिखना
steps: बच्चे एक-एक करके अपना नाम बोलते हैं।
अपने बारे में एक वाक्य बोलते हैं।
अपना नाम कॉपी में लिखने का प्रयास करते हैं।
साथी को अपना नाम पढ़कर सुनाते हैं।

levels.0: नाम बोला जाता है पर लिखने का प्रयास नहीं होता।
levels.1: नाम बोलता है और शिक्षक की मदद से कुछ अक्षर लिखता है।
levels.2: अपना नाम बोलता है, एक वाक्य कहता है और नाम लिखता है।
levels.3: नाम और एक वाक्य लिखकर साथी को पढ़कर सुनाता है।

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D4

rows.name: स्वर और व्यंजन की पहचान और लेखन (अ से ज्ञ)
steps: वर्णमाला चार्ट देखकर स्वर पढ़ते हैं।
व्यंजन अ से ज्ञ तक पढ़ते हैं।
हर वर्ण को चार पंक्तियों में लिखते हैं।
साथी के लिखे वर्ण जाँचते हैं।

levels.0: कई वर्ण उलटे या क्रम से बाहर लिखे गए हैं।
levels.1: वर्ण देखकर लिखता है, कुछ क्रम से बाहर।
levels.2: अ से ज्ञ तक सभी वर्ण क्रम से लिखे हैं।
levels.3: बिना चार्ट के क्रम से लिखता है और छूटा वर्ण बताता है।

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D4

rows.name: बिना मात्रा वाले दो, तीन, चार अक्षर के शब्द पढ़ना
steps: कार्ड पर दो अक्षर के शब्द पढ़ते हैं।
तीन अक्षर के शब्द पढ़ते हैं।
चार अक्षर के शब्द पढ़ते हैं।
एक शब्द कॉपी में लिखते हैं।

levels.0: अक्षर एक-एक करके पढ़े जाते हैं पर शब्द नहीं बनता।
levels.1: दो अक्षर के शब्द पढ़ता है, लंबे शब्दों में रुकता है।
levels.2: दो, तीन और चार अक्षर के शब्द पढ़ता है।
levels.3: नए शब्द पढ़ता है और उनसे वाक्य बनाता है।

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D4

rows.name: आ से अः की मात्राओं की पुनरावृत्ति
steps: हर मात्रा के साथ एक अक्षर बोलते हैं।
मात्रा वाले शब्द पढ़ते हैं।
पाँच शब्द मात्रा के साथ लिखते हैं।
साथी के शब्द जाँचते हैं।

levels.0: मात्राएँ अक्षर के साथ गलत जगह लिखी हैं।
levels.1: कुछ मात्राएँ सही लिखता है।
levels.2: पाँच शब्द सही मात्रा के साथ लिखे हैं।
levels.3: नए शब्द सही मात्रा के साथ लिखता है।

rows.note: named in AY 2026-27 Parent planner!D4

rows.name: हिंदी में पठन (पठण) की दिनचर्या
steps: एक छोटा गद्यांश चुनते हैं।
जोड़ी में बारी-बारी से पढ़ते हैं।
कठिन शब्द चुनकर बोर्ड पर लिखते हैं।
एक वाक्य अपने शब्दों में बताते हैं।

levels.0: शब्द अटक-अटक कर पढ़े जाते हैं।
levels.1: सरल शब्द पढ़ता है, कठिन शब्दों में मदद लेता है।
levels.2: गद्यांश साफ़ उच्चारण से पढ़ता है।
levels.3: पढ़कर एक वाक्य अपने शब्दों में बताता है।

rows.note: named in AY 2025-26 Parent planner!D37

rows.name: हिंदी में एक से बीस तक गिनती

Make a paper rocket and a launcher.
Launch and measure how far it goes.
Change one thing and launch again.

source.cell: PROJECT - Make a paper rocket launcher

rows.note: named in Grade 2 _August planner 2024.pdf!PROJECT - Make a paper rocket launcher

levels.0: Rocket is made but does not launch.
levels.1: Launches after help setting up.
levels.2: Launches and measures the distance.
levels.3: Changes one thing and explains the new distance.

rows.name: Blow the ball: changing speed
steps: Talk about what makes things go faster or slower.
Blow a ball gently and then harder along a table.
Say what changed.
Draw the result.

source.cell: Changing speed - Activity: Blow the ball

rows.note: named in Grade 2 _August planner 2024.pdf!Changing speed - Activity: Blow the ball

levels.0: Blows the ball with no comment on what happened.
levels.1: Says the ball moved faster after a hard blow when asked.
levels.2: Compares gentle and hard blows and what happened to the speed.
levels.3: Predicts the effect of a third blow and tests it.

rows.name: Feel the force: changing direction
steps: Push a ball and watch where it goes.
Push it sideways to make it turn.
Predict with a drawing where it will go.
Check the prediction.

source.cell: Changing direction Activity - Feel the force

rows.note: named in Grade 2 _August planner 2024.pdf!Changing direction Activity - Feel the force

levels.0: Pushes in different ways without noting where the ball goes.
levels.1: Notes the direction after a push when prompted.
levels.2: Predicts with a drawing and checks it.
levels.3: Explains why a push from the side changed the path.

rows.name: Stretching rubber bands: finding patterns in results
steps: Stretch a rubber band by different amounts.
Record how far an object moves.
Look for a pattern in the results.
Say how a force changes shape.

source.cell: Finding patterns in results - rubber bands

rows.note: named in Grade 2 _August planner 2024.pdf!Finding patterns in results - rubber bands

levels.0: Stretches the band but records nothing.
levels.1: Records two results with help.
levels.2: Records several results and notes a pattern.
levels.3: Explains the pattern and predicts a new result.

rows.name: Family shadows with brush strokes and knife painting
steps: Look at a shadow outline of a family member.
Paint it with brush strokes.
Add texture with a palette knife.
Say what the strokes show.
rows.note: named in Grade 2 _August planner 2024.pdf!Visual Arts: Family shadows

levels.0: Paint covers the paper without a shape.
levels.1: Paints an outline with help.
levels.2: Paints the shadow with brush and knife strokes.
levels.3: Describes how the two tools change the look.

rows.name: Rhythm games: Pass the Beat and Rhythm Round Robin
steps: Clap a simple beat together.
Pass the beat around the circle.
Play Rhythm Round Robin with body percussion or classroom instruments.
Add a new pattern.
rows.note: named in Grade 2 _August planner 2024.pdf!Music: Rhythm and Beat Mastery

levels.0: Beat is lost when passed to the next child.
levels.1: Keeps the beat with the educator leading.
levels.2: Passes the beat on time around the circle.
levels.3: Makes up a pattern and others repeat it.

rows.name: Continent boxes with pictures and objects
steps: Pick a continent such as Asia or Africa.
Collect pictures and objects linked to it.
Put them in a box.
Show the box and say what is inside.
rows.note: named in Grade 2 _August planner 2024.pdf!Geography - Continents: continent boxes

levels.0: Box holds items with no link to the continent.
levels.1: Names the continent and one item.
levels.2: Box has pictures and objects that fit the continent.
levels.3: Explains why each item belongs to the continent.

rows.name: Field visit to the post office
steps: Prepare questions to ask.
Visit and watch how letters are handled.
Draw the steps a letter takes.
Share one thing learned.

rows.note: named in Grade 2 _August planner 2024.pdf!Events: Field Visit to Post Office

levels.0: Drawing does not show how a letter travels.

levels.2: Draws the steps a letter takes in order.
levels.3: Explains why each step is needed.

rows.name: Mirror, Mirror: naming good things I do
steps: Look into a mirror in turn.
Say one good thing you do.
Add a second good quality.
Listen to others and say one good thing about someone else.
rows.note: named in Grade 2 _August planner 2024.pdf!Unit 1 - Respect: Mirror, Mirror lesson
look_fors: Says one good thing they do when asked.
Names a second quality aloud.
Listens while others take their turn.

rows.name: Lily the Leopard: respecting that we are different
steps: Listen to the story of Lily the Leopard.
Say how Lily was different from the other leopards.
Name a quality Lily has.
Talk about why each person is valued.
rows.note: named in Grade 2 _August planner 2024.pdf!Unit 1 - Respect: objectives
look_fors: Says how the character was different.
Names one quality of the character.
Listens without interrupting during the talk.
